issues.en: As part of underwriting studies for insurance placement, Nathan visited prospective companies to discuss their safety process to determine their overall risk status. In retrospect, what he was doing was an attempt to determine through observation of the various artifacts and discussions about the espoused values, as evidenced by mission statements, policies, procedures, and so on, the status and strength of the safety culture. In these reviews, the underwriters want to know: “Is this prospective Insured maintaining a safe work environment and is it serious about keeping hazards and associated risk under control?” If the observed artifacts indicate that issues exist that increased the potential for loss-producing events and did not reflect the espoused values, then the underlying belief system was different from the espoused values. An example, an espoused value was inspections to be done routinely and deficiencies immediately corrected. If observations were noted that there were maintenance and housekeeping problems, then the real belief was inspections were not considered significant. An organization with a good safety culture relies on the close interdependence between fundamental safety and organizational processes. In practice, a high level of safety culture means the systematic organization and implementation of activities aimed at creating high quality technical, human, and organizational systems. Management of Safety, Safety Culture, and Self Assessment (2000)
issues.ko:
기업 보험 인수를 위한 언더라이팅 실사 조사의 일환으로, 네이선은 기업들의 전반적인 위험(Risk) 상태를 객관적으로 평가하기 위해 안전 프로세스를 점검하러 여러 유망 기업들을 현장 방문했다. 

돌이켜보면, 대부분의 경영진은 자신들의 안전 프로그램이 얼마나 훌륭한지 번지르르하게 자랑하곤 했다. 그러나 현장 라운딩을 단 10분만 돌아보아도 경영진의 말과 현장의 실체 사이에는 하늘과 땅 차이의 거대한 간극이 존재함을 즉시 간파할 수 있었다. 

비상구는 물건들로 꽉 막혀 있었고, 근로자들은 보호안경을 턱에 걸치고 있었으며, 기계의 인터록 방호장치는 작업 속도를 올린다는 핑계로 테이프로 묶여 해제되어 있었다. 

경영진이 믿고 있는 안전과 현장 작업자들이 매일매일 체감하고 실행하는 안전 사이의 이 치명적인 단절이야말로 조직문화가 병들어 있다는 가장 강력한 증거였다.

issues.en: Habits are defined as “an acquired behavior pattern regularly followed until it has become almost involuntary, i.e., the habit of looking both ways before crossing the street” (Habit, 2018). As culture involves patterns of behavior, unless old beliefs that allow at-risk behaviors to be acceptable are eliminated, unsafe activities become habitual norms and will continue to exist. Duhigg suggests that an understanding of what he calls “keystone habits” is needed. Keystone habits have the “power to start a chain reaction, changing other habits as they move through an organization.” Duhigg states that these keystone habits “start a process that, over time, transforms everything” (Duhigg, 2012). Duhigg believes that “the habits that matter most are the ones that, when they start to shift, dislodge, and remake other patterns” (Duhigg, 2012). Changing a keystone habit impacts the culture and in turn, changes an entire organization. Duhigg used the example of how Alcoa began changing its overall culture in the late 1980s. The new CEO, Paul O’Neill, wanted to improve the way Alcoa did business by improving its quality and methods of production. O’Neill used a strong emphasis on Alcoa’s safety program to create keystone habits to change poor organizational traits that impacted the entire corporation. Alcoa built a robust safety process that in turn improved the overall performance of its operations. During this period, safety became an ingrained habit and underlying value that remained in place long after O’Neill left Alcoa. As of 2013, Alcoa’s safety and health programs remain healthy and robust (Benton, 2017; Cable, 2014; Ross, 2012). Cultures grow out of the Keystone habits in every organization, whether leaders are aware of them or not…. Keystone habits transform us by creating cultures that make clear the values that, in the heat of a difficult decision or a moment of uncertainty, we might otherwise forget. Charles Duhigg, “Power of Habit” (Duhigg, 2012) In this case, the CEO went straight to the core of Alcoa’s assumptions and beliefs. An assumption existed that safety was unrelated to other issues impacting the success of the organization. By realizing safety-related matters touched on all areas of the organization he was able to begin the process of changing underlying beliefs by creating a different series of key habits.
issues.ko:
습관(Habits)이란 "거의 무의식적이고 반사적인 행동이 될 때까지 규칙적으로 반복 실행됨으로써 후천적으로 획득된 행동 패턴, 예컨대 길을 건너기 전에 좌우를 살피는 습관"으로 정의된다 (Habits, 2018). 

조직문화는 본질적으로 **'조직 구성원들의 습관들의 거대한 총합'**이다. 

안전한 작업 습관이든 불안전한 지름길(Shortcut) 습관이든, 습관은 오랜 세월에 걸쳐 형성되며 한 번 굳어지면 쉽게 바뀌지 않는다. 

찰스 두히그(Charles Duhigg)가 그의 명저 『습관의 힘(The Power of Habit)』에서 갈파했듯이, 모든 습관은 **'신호(Cue) - 루틴(Routine) - 보상(Reward)'**이라는 습관의 고리(Habit loop)를 따라 작동한다. 

작업자가 공정을 진행할 때 시간 압박이라는 '신호'가 주어지면, 안전 절차를 건너뛰고 방호장치를 해제하는 '루틴'을 밟고, 그 결과 작업을 빨리 끝내고 관리자에게 지적받지 않는다는 '보상'을 얻게 된다면, 이 위험한 불법적 일탈은 즉시 강력한 조직적 습관으로 고착화된다. 

안전문화를 바꾼다는 것은 바로 이러한 일상적 작업 습관의 고리를 정밀하게 해체하고, 안전한 행동이 즉각적인 인정과 보상으로 연결되는 새로운 선순환 루틴을 구축하는 것을 의미한다.

issues.en: When determining the nature of organizational culture, each aspect of the culture must be assessed to determine the driving characteristics of the organization and how they are interconnected. With this understanding, the potential for shaping the safety culture is enhanced, and the required time frame for change may be decreased. This will be discussed in more detail in Chapter 4. Knowing the type of management style provides insights on how to approach and work with leadership. Refer Table 2.2 for an outline of the types of cultures suggested by several authors. The styles followed by each of these authors appear to have similar characteristics and support an overall theme. After understanding the type of culture, the safety management system is designed to match the culture. This further understanding aides in a more proficient communication approach to leadership. For example, developing an employee participative approach has less chance of success if the leadership culture is authoritarian. As a cautionary note, these definitions represent a spectrum of types and are not hard and fast boundaries. A further complication is that general styles may change as leadership or conditions evolve or also change.
issues.ko:
조직문화의 본질적 성격을 규명할 때, 조직을 실질적으로 움직이는 핵심 추진 특성들이 무엇이며 그러한 특성들이 조직 내의 다양한 부서 및 계층 간에 어떻게 상호 연결되어 있는지를 파악하기 위해 문화의 모든 측면들이 다각도로 평가되어야 한다. 

조직은 단일한 성격만을 띠지 않는다. 어떤 조직은 권위주의적이고 처벌 위주인 반면, 어떤 조직은 자율적이고 협력적이다. 

이러한 문화적 성격은 안전을 대하는 구성원들의 태도를 결정짓는 가장 핵심적인 렌즈가 된다.

issues.en: The effects of a silo mentality reduce efficiency in providing an overall safe operation and contribute to the degrading of the safety culture. As the safety professional must span across the organization, the safety management system can help break down barriers by sharing and encouraging communication once the silo mentality has been broken down. The solution we devised was a “team of teams,” an organization within which the relationships between constituent teams resembled those between individuals on a single team: teams that had traditionally resided in separate silos would now have to become fused to one another vis trust and purpose. McChrystal, Fussell, Collins, and Silverman (2015)
issues.ko:
사일로 멘탈리티가 미치는 악영향은 전반적인 안전 운영을 달성하는 효율성을 저하시키며 안전문화를 부식시키고 퇴행시키는 데 결정적인 역할을 한다. 

안전 전문가는 조직의 모든 경계를 넘나들며 협력해야 하기 때문에, 부서 간의 장벽은 치명적인 안전 위험요인 정보를 가로막는 재앙의 온상이 된다. 

이를 극복하지 못하면 안전은 각자도생의 고립된 섬으로 전락하고 만다 (그림 2.4 참조).

issues.en: What activities are currently being stressed that is not mission-essential to the safety management system? Refer Table 2.4 for the extremes that might be found between positive and negative cultures. Although these elements are written with a school in mind, a similar thought holds for general industry: A key question is, can culture be shaped by leadership, or is it so amorphous and unalterable that it has a life of its own? Although school culture is deeply embedded in the hearts and minds of staff, students, and parents, it can be shaped by the work of leaders. As this book demonstrates, one of the key tasks of leaders is shaping culture through a myriad of daily interactions, careful reflection, and conscious efforts. Deal and Peterson (2002)

현재 안전경영시스템의 진정한 사명 필수 과업이 아님에도 불구하고 불필요하게 강조되고 낭비되고 있는 활동들은 무엇인가? 

긍정적인 안전문화와 부정적인 안전문화 사이에 존재하는 극단적인 차이점들에 대해서는 표 2.4를 참조하라.

issues.en: A strategy is needed on how to present finding for improving the safety management system to the leadership team. An understanding of the overall “political” climate is needed which is why a detailed review of the current history of the safety process is necessary. What actions can be taken immediately to increase the potential to shape the safety culture of an organization? A gap analysis will describe the current organizational culture, its characteristics, and traits. The following questions must be addressed before attempting to modify or change the safety culture:
issues.ko:
안전경영시스템을 개선하기 위한 현장 진단 결과와 발견점들을 리더십 팀에 어떻게 설득력 있게 제시할 것인가에 대한 정교한 전략이 요구된다. 

사내의 전반적인 '정치적(Political)' 기후에 대한 깊은 이해가 필수적이며, 이는 리더십이 안전 권고사항을 어떻게 받아들일 것인가를 좌우한다. 

격차 분석(Gap Analysis)을 성공적으로 수행하기 위해 다음과 같은 세 가지 핵심 질문을 반드시 던져야 한다:

issues.en:
* What does the organization value?
* How are priorities established within the organization?
* What is the status of the current safety culture? Gather as much information about the organization as possible as well as
the perception, effectiveness, and inclusion of safety-related activities?
* Does the perception and assessment of the current safety culture match that of organizational leadership?
* Does a gap exist between what the employees and leadership believe?
* What are the “mandates” of leadership?
* What is the safety process mission? Does it develop, sustain, or improve the safety culture?
* What structures and processes are needed to ensure that the safety culture can be maintained in the organization?
* How are quality, production, finance, human resources, and so on, managed within the organization? Is safety managed
similarly?
* How are employees trained, educated, and oriented to the desired norms and values of the organizations? Is training
adequate for the scope of risk and hazards?
* Are safety concepts considered part of these norms and values?
* How are safety responsibilities and expected behaviors communicated and enforced within the organization?
* Is information about critical, uncontrolled hazards or associated risks communicated to the leadership team in a format
that matches their current communication style?
* Does the leadership team understand what is being communicated and its potential consequences?
* Are hazards and associated risk accepted too low in the organization?
The gap analysis should include a thorough understanding of the organization’s current culture’s state and the desired future state of the culture. From this assessment, a strategy for change can be developed. Depending on the leadership mandate, an initial strategy would be to continue to maintain the existing safety process and its programs while communications are established, and the information is gathered on what is needed to be changed. Nonetheless, action should be taken when severe or life-threatening conditions are found that need immediate change. The challenge is ensuring that serious and life-threatening situations are immediately communicated to those making decisions.

issues.en:
The implementation, sustaining, or improvement of a safety culture requires an almost Sherlock Holmes-like ability to use observation and logic to identify what, where, and how underlying organizational characteristics and traits impact the safety management system. Just as the fictional character Sherlock Holmes (Sherlock Holmes, 2018). Culture is the result of the long-term experience of the organization regarding successful problem-solving, various personalities, conditions related to both past and present. If the leadership team desires to improve the safety process, it must ensure that its message has been defined by clear intent and expectations. Safety is the interaction that results from:
* Organizational beliefs, values, and structure.
* Processes and operational elements.
* Skills and knowledge of the people hired to use those processes and operational elements.
* The leadership team and its desires and goals.
* The social and physical environment necessary to reach its stated goals. The reason for its existence.
The safety management system should be evaluated for overall efficient design and structure that matches the organization’s overall operational structure with its inherent hazards and associated risks. An understanding of how “Culture” is defined and the application of this understanding provides insights on how all the aspects of the organization fit together as discussed in Chapter 1.
issues.ko:
안전문화의 성공적인 실행, 흔들림 없는 유지, 그리고 지속적인 개선을 달성하기 위해서는 셜록 홈즈(Sherlock Holmes)와도 같은 날카로운 관찰력과 치밀한 논리력이 요구된다. 

즉 눈에 보이는 피상적인 현상 너머에서 기저의 기본 가정들이 도대체 **무엇이며, 어디에 숨어 있고, 어떻게 작동하는지**를 식별해 내는 탐정의 직관이 필요하다. 

문화를 깊이 이해한다는 것은 조직의 고유한 개성을 파악하고, 그 속에서 안전경영시스템이 어떻게 조화롭게 작동할 수 있는지를 알아내는 것이다. 

문화는 고정불변의 화석이 아니다. 에드거 샤인의 3수준 모델(인공물, 표방된 가치, 기저의 기본 가정)을 체계적인 진단 도구로 활용하고, INPO의 9가지 경고 깃발을 엄격한 조기 경보 지표로 삼아 현장의 맹점을 끊임없이 교정해 나갈 때 비로소 진정한 고신뢰 안전문화가 뿌리내릴 수 있다.

issues.en:
1. Explain why understanding the organizational culture is essential to increase the potential for the effective development and implementation of a safety process.
2. What is organizational culture? Why is it considered essential to the development of an effective safety management
system?
3. Discuss the components of organizational culture as outlined in Table 2.1. Explain why they are important to the safety
management system.
4. Compare and contrast the three levels of culture. Explain why it is important to understand these concepts.
5. Explain the patterns of behavior that create habits in a safety culture.
6. Determine the nature of a culture you have worked in. Consider each aspect of the culture that is involved in driving
personalities and characteristics of the organization and how they are interconnected.
7. Refer Table 2.3, Getting a Feel for an Organization, and list the elements that are discussed. Provide some additional
items to this list based on your experience. Explain how this influences the safety management system and the safety culture.
8. Organizational cultures can vary from department to department, even from a plant to plant. A further complication
occurs when a company has various international entities. Explain how cultural misunderstandings might develop.
9. Leadership sets the business priorities for the many activities necessary to accomplish its primary organizational
mission which is survival in its niche in the marketplace. Explain why this is important to define the “missionessential” safety activities.
10. List the nine warning flag factors that can defeat successful implementation of a safety management system. What
strategy would you follow to overcome them? Where would you begin?

issues.en: A Safety Professional’s positions must be perceived as professional and trustworthy. A network can be destroyed in one brief, unguarded moment of anger or being found to be unreliable. Politicians and actors have destroyed their careers in a matter of seconds by making a comment or gesture revealing their real character. Refer Fig. 3.2, for an example of how influence moves three degrees. Everything we do or say tends to ripple through our network, having an impact on our friends (one degree), our friends’ friends (two degrees), and even our friends’ friends (three degrees). Our influence gradually dissipates and ceases to have a noticeable effect on people beyond…three degrees of separation. Christakis and Fowler (2009)
issues.ko:
안전 전문가의 직무와 위치는 반드시 전문적이고 깊이 신뢰할 수 있는 것으로 지각되어야 한다. 

수년에 걸쳐 힘들게 쌓아 올린 신뢰의 네트워크라 할지라도, 단 한 번의 방심한 분노의 폭발이나 약속을 지키지 않는 무책임한 모습이 드러나는 순간 단 일초 만에 산산조각 날 수 있다. 

전문적 평판과 진정성을 흔들림 없이 유지하는 것은 네트워크의 생명력을 지탱하는 절대적 산소이다.

issues.en:
The goal of a network is to be able to transmit reliable, proven, and validated safety concepts and techniques through an organization in a manner that enhances the safety culture. An analogy is to view communication as taking the form of a virus that can be carried throughout the organizational body. Additional, safety communications should match the style and format used by the organization if the information is to engage employees and the leadership team. Brodie outlines a concept of thoughts and messages being viewed as a virus in his book “Virus of the Mind” (Brodie, 2009). According to Dawkins (2006), a meme is a packet of information providing a short burst of information understood by the intended audience (Solon, 2013). Communication should be regarded as an attempt to develop a meme. The meme or specific packet of information, once accepted, can then be further transmitted to others or if rejected, not go anywhere, mainly allowed to die by the recipient. “A meme is a unit of information in a mind whose existence influences events such that more copies of itself get created in other minds” (Brodie, 2009). and validated? What safety memes can you identify? Do we have resilient safety memes which persist even though they have not been proven In safety management, memes tell people what to do and how to complete specific procedures and methods. When work conditions remain the same, hazards and associated risk may stay under control using a series of memes that quickly tell people what to do. Obsolete memes may continue to be used even when they no longer work in the current work environment or culture. A meme that works for one organization, a location, or department may or may not be followed by another similar entity. According to Brodie, several types of memes exist. A “distinctive meme” is one that describes, classifies, or labels something (Brodie, 2009). A safety meme and at-risk behavior meme labels something as safe versus unsafe. The word “safety” is an example of an information packet carrying specific information. “Be Safe” transmits a range of suggested behaviors depending on the work environment. A safety meme has such incredible strength; it may not be clearly defined given everyone assumes they know what is meant by “safety.” The safety meme may or may not have the same connotation between individuals, groups, or organizations. If a safety meme is to have influence, it must be replicable, become a mind virus, and be collectively defined. Ideally, employees without coercion readily transfer their safety knowledge to other employees if a safety meme is present. The second type of meme discussed is the “Strategy Meme” (Brodie, 2009). The strategy meme transmits information about what to do under specific conditions. If a certain behavior is necessary to prevent an injury, a “cause and effect” is created, for example. If “X” is done this specific way, then the task will remain “safe,” as defined by the strategy meme. Another kind of meme is a strategy. A kind of floating rule of thumb that tells you what to do when you come across an applicable situation to achieve some desired result. Brodie (2009) An existing meme will continue to stress the use of previously acceptable behavior that may be no longer “safe.” Some examples include new procedures for startup of new equipment, starting a different production process, driving a new or different vehicle. The old meme defining how to do the task may still be mentally in effect and increase the potential for injury or damage. For example, after moving into a new house and going into a room, the operative meme signals to reach for a light switch on the left, only to find the switch is not there. In the new house, the switch is in a different location. The light switch meme from the old house is still in active use in your mind. Brodie’s “Association Meme” links various memes together (Brodie, 2009). When the information in one packet of information is activated, it activates other information. An example of how this can create an unsafe situation is the meme, “Where there’s smoke, there’s fire.” For Example, When people make assumptions, a meme is driving the action. When searching for the source of “smoke,” the immediate thought is “Where there’s smoke, there’s fire?” What if it’s not smoke but a harmful chemical vapor? Inhalation of chemical vapors can cause serious physical injury or possibly long-term health effects. The meme sets up the assumption, “smoke equals fire.” What appears to be “smoke” may be something else. Brodie suggests a good meme is spread without difficulty throughout a population. He suggests three ways to get a meme to penetrate and take hold (Brodie, 2009):
* Conditioning, Repetition of the same message. A form of this type of conditioning is used in the Activity-Based Safety
System (ABSS) which will be discussed in detail in Chapter 11. ABSS consist of safety procedures, preshift reviews, or work activity such as daily, weekly, and monthly activities, all intended to help instill a specific conditioned response necessary to help with hazard and associated risk controls. The idea is to be consistent with the message.
* Cognitive Dissonance, “Creates mental pressure and resolving it.” Building a case for an improved safety culture
creates a dissonance between where the organization is now in an undesirable condition and a vision of where it could be. Cognitive Dissonance, “In modern psychology, cognitive dissonance is the feeling of discomfort when simultaneously holding two or more conflicting cognitions: ideas, beliefs, values, or emotional reactions” (Cognitive dissonance, 2018; Foster, 2018). Defining and establishing a vision and mission of what the safety culture could be and setting goals and objectives creates cognitive dissonance, mental pressure. If the safety meme is strong enough, it replaces the old memes that accepted lower standards and at-risk habits or behavior.
* Trojan Horse, Is a leading meme and when publicized it triggers the advancement of several obscured memes. For
example, as we discussed in Chapter 2, Alcoa used a safety meme as the mechanism to improve its culture of quality, creativity, and customer relations (Duhigg, 2012). Refer Fig. 3.3 as an example of memes move from mind to mind.

네트워크의 궁극적 목표는 검증되고 입증되었으며 신뢰할 수 있는 안전 개념과 기법들을 안전문화를 고도화하는 방식으로 조직 전체에 강력하게 전파하는 데 있다. 

생생한 비유를 들자면, 커뮤니케이션을 조직이라는 거대한 신체 전반으로 퍼져나가는 일종의 **'바이러스(Virus)'**의 형태로 바라보는 것이다. 

또한 안전 커뮤니케이션은 그 정보가 일선 직원과 리더십 팀 모두를 능동적으로 몰입시키기 위해 조직이 평소 사용하는 고유한 스타일 및 형식과 완벽히 부합해야 한다. 

리처드 브로디(Richard Brodie)는 그의 명저 『마음의 바이러스(Virus of the Mind)』에서 인간의 생각과 메시지가 마음과 마음을 감염시키는 바이러스로 간주될 수 있다는 혁신적인 개념을 개괄했다 (Brodie, 2009). 

리처드 도킨스(Dawkins, 2006)에 따르면, **'밈(Meme)'**이란 대상 청중에게 직관적으로 명쾌하게 이해되는 짧고 강력한 정보의 패킷(A packet of information providing a short burst of information)을 의미한다 (Solon, 2013). 

모든 안전 커뮤니케이션은 강력한 안전 밈(Safety Meme)을 창출하려는 전략적 시도로 간주되어야 한다. 

특정한 정보 패킷인 밈은 한 번 상대방에게 수용되면 타인들에게 폭발적으로 재전파될 수 있으며, 반대로 거부당할 경우 수신자에 의해 더 이상 어디로도 퍼져나가지 못하고 그 자리에서 쓸쓸히 소멸하고 만다. 

"밈이란 한 사람의 뇌에서 다른 사람의 뇌로 모방을 통해 복제되고 전달되는 문화 전달의 기본 단위이다." — 리처드 도킨스 (Dawkins, 2006). 

안전 분야에서 오랜 세월 동안 전수되어 온 수많은 슬로건들은 본질적으로 일종의 안전 밈이다. 그러나 그 밈이 긍정적이고 실천적인 행동을 낳는 건강한 밈인지, 아니면 오히려 복지부동과 형식주의를 조장하는 악성 밈인지를 날카롭게 분별해야 한다.

In completing a social network map, an effort is made to discover “Peripheral People,” Individuals outside direct networks or, while part of the organization, considered “Mavericks” operating independently outside the organizational network norm (Christakis & Fowler, 2009). As they are outside the normal flow of information, these individuals may not be using up-to-date risk information and be following outdated safety criteria. The basic nature and type of questions asked include:
* Does your network map show or imply communication gaps?
* Do you have links in place with each level of the leadership team?
* Are all employees able to quickly link with you?
* Can a critical hazard or associated risk message rapidly get to the level of leadership appropriate to the potential severity which
must be addressed? (Catastrophic examples from history include the Challenger and Columbia space shuttles, the BP Gulf Horizon.) Literature will show the failure of the communication flow created a catastrophic loss.
* What are the primary types of communication used by the organization?
* What is the strength of your relationship with the leadership team and employees?
* Are all your communications positive and two way?
* What actions can you take to improve or how can the relationship be repaired and improved?
* Are you centrally located and directly connected to leadership by no more than three degrees of separation?

사회연결망 맵을 완성하는 과정에서 반드시 찾아내야 할 또 하나의 결정적인 그룹은 바로 **'주변부 사람들(Peripheral People)'**이다. 

이들은 직접적인 네트워크의 외곽에 머물러 있거나, 비록 조직의 구성원이기는 하지만 주류 집단에 동화되지 않는 **'이단아(Mavericks)'**나 **'아웃사이더(Outsiders)'**로 취급받는 인물들이다 (Christakis & Fowler, 2009). 

주변부 사람들은 흔히 비사교적이거나, 까다롭거나, 불만이 많거나, 엉뚱한 괴짜로 낙인찍혀 소외되곤 한다. 

그러나 네트워크 이론의 거대한 반전은, 진정으로 독창적이고 파괴적인 혁신과 조직의 치명적인 맹점(Blind spots)에 대한 경고 신호가 주류 집단 내부가 아니라 바로 이 '주변부 사람들'로부터 터져 나온다는 사실이다! 

그들은 조직의 집단사고(Groupthink)에 물들지 않았기 때문에 현장의 불안전한 관행과 시스템적 모순을 가장 날카롭고 솔직하게 꿰뚫어 볼 수 있다. 현명한 안전 전문가는 이 주변부 사람들을 소외시키지 않고 적극적으로 접촉하여 그들의 고유한 시각을 안전 진단의 귀중한 자산으로 포용한다.

When organizations analyze risks or risk events, the information gathered is disseminated throughout the organization to leadership, engineering, departments being impacted, safety professionals, and other specialist and technical experts. Risk perception is based upon one’s experience, social, environmental judgments (Lowrance, 1976). The planning process ranges from daily, weekly, monthly, annual, and multiyear planning. 이러한 파이프라인의 병목과 왜곡을 타파하고, 현장의 적나라한 재해(Hazard)와 위험(Risk) 정보가 필터링 없이 실시간으로 최고 의사결정권자에게 직통으로 도달할 수 있는 투명한 바이패스 소통망을 구축하는 것이야말로 안전 전문가의 핵심 사명이다.

issues.en: The safety culture is dependent on how well safety information is communicated. Personal and organizational networks determine the quality of safety management system information and how quickly it can move through an organization. The quality of information and its value to the leadership team and employees establishes the perception of safety and its influence on the safety culture. An organizational chart provides a road map of describing the hierarchy of reporting relationships and responsibilities, who reports to who, where they are, what they do. The organizational chart can be in constant change as personnel is promoted, operational structure changes completed, and new responsibilities assigned. It needs to update routinely. Designing and improving both personal and organizational networks to better communicate information increases the potential of a quality safety culture. The goal of a network is to be able to rapidly transmit reliable, proven, and validated safety concepts and techniques through an organization in a manner that enhances the safety culture. An analogy is to view communication as taking the form of a virus that can be carried throughout the organizational body. A Social Network Map connects topics, individuals and ideas, and relationships. A map is developed using three components as building blocks. Social network analysis shows individuals or groups and the connections between them. The safety function is a specialized discipline providing a depth and scope of knowledge and information of significant benefit to the entire organization.

안전문화의 성패는 안전 정보가 사내에서 얼마나 투명하고 신속하게 소통되는가에 전적으로 의존한다. 

개인적 네트워크와 공식 조직 구조는 안전경영시스템 정보의 질적 수준을 결정짓는 절대적 요소이다. 

우리는 모두 개인적·전문적 네트워크의 복잡한 그물망의 일부이며, 이 네트워크는 우리가 미처 알지 못하는 3단계의 거리까지 파동처럼 영향력을 미친다. 

공식 조직도의 한계를 직시하고 보이지 않는 비공식 네트워크와 밈(Memes)의 역학을 꿰뚫어 보아야 한다. 단순하고(Simple), 의외성이 있으며(Unexpected), 구체적이고(Concrete), 신뢰할 수 있으며(Credible), 감성을 울리고(Emotional), 생생한 스토리(Story)를 담은 강력한 안전 밈을 조직의 파이프라인에 주입하라. 

중심 연결자, 경계 연결자, 정보 브로커의 역할을 자임하고 소외된 주변부 사람들의 솔직한 경고음에 귀를 기울일 때, 안전은 비로소 조직 전체를 움직이는 살아있는 문화로 승화될 것이다.

issues.en: Initial safety concepts were developed at the beginning of the 20th century, and its principles were based on new methods for improving productivity in manufacturing. Fredrick Taylor’s Principles of Scientific Management were adapted for use in safety programming (Frederick Winslow Taylor, 1919). At the time of Taylor’s “Scientific Management,” most jobs were primarily manual with limited safety efforts built into the process. For example, Taylor believed that by analyzing a job task by breaking it into its components, its efficiency could be increased. In retrospect, the Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) is based on Taylor’s concepts by going through the same process and identifying the hazards in each task. This traditional JHA approach does not incorporate concepts of risk and does not take into account how the majority of jobs are now designed. The use of Using the Job Hazard Analysis will be discussed in detail in Chapter 12. Taylor’s identities four principles as follows: Replace working by “rule of thumb,” or simple habit and common sense, and instead, use the scientific method to study work and determine the most efficient way to perform specific tasks. Rather than simply assign workers to just any job, match workers to their jobs based on capability and motivation, and train them to work at maximum efficiency. Monitor worker performance, and provide instructions and supervision to ensure that they’re using the most efficient ways of working. Allocate the work between managers and workers so that the managers spend their time planning and training, allowing the workers to perform their tasks efficiently. Frederick Taylor and Scientific Management, Understanding Taylorism and Early Management Theory (2017) When traditional safety programs are reviewed, a vestige of Taylor’s four principles become apparent. General McChrystal notes, that “…most industries have subscribed to management doctrines…similar to Fredrick Taylor’s “Scientific Management,” a system that is excellent for achieving highly efficient execution of known, repeatable processes at scale.” (McChrystal et al., 2015) McChrystal calls this a “structure and culture of disciplined, stratified reductionism.” In reviewing basic job tasks, these methods may remain valid. Technology and changes in the workforce require different concepts of thinking about safety management. Taylor’s Scientific Management Theory promotes the idea that there is “one right way” to do something. As such, it is at odds with current approaches such as Management By Objectives (MBO), Continuous Improvement initiatives, Business Process Reengineering (BPR), and other tools like them. These promote individual responsibility, and seek to push decision making through all levels of the organization. Frederick Taylor and scientific management, understanding taylorism and early management theory (2017) As organizations and operations have become more complex per McChrystal, “Efficiency is no longer enough.” Taylor developed methods to improve job tasks whose outcome was predictable. His methods were not a systems approach designed to consider all the interconnections and dynamics of the organization. A shift has to be made from dealing strictly with “complicated challenges,” programs, guidelines, specific tasks, having predictable outcomes to a different situation of dealing with the complexity of the various system interactions with potential unpredictable outcomes and evolving networks. The design of a safety management system attempts to holistically approach and assess the complexity of an organization to better manage the overall safety process. Unfortunately, the continuing perception of safety as being a simple process still exist, and the methods used not complicated or requiring much planning.

근대적 안전 개념은 20세기 초반에 태동하기 시작했으며, 그 기본 원리는 당시 새롭게 등장했던 공학적 분석 기법과 현대 산업 경영 이론에 깊은 뿌리를 두고 있었다. 그 시기는 프레더릭 윈슬로 테일러(Frederick Winslow Taylor)의 과학적 관리법이 전 산업계를 지배하던 시대였다. 테일러의 이론은 철저한 관찰, 시간 및 동작 연구(Time and Motion Studies), 그리고 직무를 표준화된 최소 단위로 쪼개는 작업 표준화를 통해 노동 생산성을 극대화하는 데 초점을 맞추었다 (Taylor, 1911).

이러한 고전적 분석 접근법은 생산성 향상에는 기여했으나, 인간을 마치 기계의 한 부품처럼 취급하는 환원주의적 한계를 지니고 있었다. 복잡한 시스템으로서의 조직을 이해하지 못한 채 개별 부품이나 단편적인 작업 동작만을 뜯어고치려 했던 초기 안전 프로그램의 유산은, 오늘날까지도 많은 현장에서 안전을 '단순한 규정 준수'나 '체크리스트 작성' 수준으로 협소하게 바라보게 만드는 부작용을 낳았다.

진정한 안전 프로세스는 테일러 식의 단순 기계적 통제를 넘어, 전체 시스템의 복잡성과 인간적 요소를 온전히 포용하는 현대적 시스템 사고(Systems Thinking)로 진화해야만 한다.

issues.en:
The Cons of a safety management system requires that an ongoing process is maintained and constantly monitored. The safety management system may have problems if:
* It is not implemented properly and appears to be a “canned” approach not integrated with other management processes,
that is, it provides espoused values but is not guiding the organization.
* Its scope is too narrowly implemented and is viewed as a series of one-off programs and not as an interconnected holistic
process.
* A false sense of safety can develop if the measurement of its activities and process is not conscientiously and consistently followed. An honest, comprehensive, and routine appraisal system must be in place to ensure “pencil whipping,”
false documentation, is not occurring.
* Consequences are not in place for both good and poor implementation. If some form of valued recognition is not present,
employees may see the process as just another administrative task or paperwork to be dispensed with.
* It may be perceived as too time consuming and the why of the safety management system not fully understood. As stated
previously and we want to reenforce the concept, the traditional methods of safety program success are dependent on OSHA recordability and frequency of loss-producing events. If the perception of “no loss no risk” is present then the attitude may be “we don’t need to do this!,” even if associated risks are high.
* It is not customized to the organization and does not consider the organizational structure and existing culture which
may reject, or worse, only espouse, but not internalize the process. Examples of Governmental and Voluntary-Related Safety Management Systems Safety management systems are divided into two types, governmental-regulatory related, either mandated or voluntary systems developed by national and internationally recognized standards agencies and professional societies. Government-related programs emphasize the administration of regulations. This section provides an overview of several safety management systems to demonstrate the various formats and elements. An awareness of the formats can aid in the decision on which safety management system best fits an organization. Safety management systems can be international, national, or state/province/city. Many states and provinces have suggested or mandated safety management systems. Various professional, standards or interdisciplinary groups or societies may offer standards. Finally, an organization may have developed and implemented its process. The following are examples of several standardized governmental-related guidelines safety management systems:
* The Federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs
(Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs General Industry and Construction, 2017)
* The Federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration Voluntary Prevention Program (Voluntary Protection
Protection (VPP), 2016)
* The U.S. Department of Energy Voluntary Protection Program (Voluntary Protection Protection (DOE-VPP), 2016)
State or Providence systems include:
* The California OSHA Injury and Illness Prevention Program Title 8-§3203 (Guide to developing your workplace injury
and illness prevention program with checklists for self-inspection, 2016). California OSHA mandates a formal approach to safety program management.
* Building an Effective Health and Safety management system (2015), Partnerships in Injury Reduction, Alberta.
* An interesting approach was taken by the State of Montana with its mandated Montana Safety Culture Act (Job safety
analysis, 2018; Safety Culture Act, 2015). Refer to Appendix 6.2 for the Mandated Safety Culture Act standard, a relevant public domain document that can be downloaded and used for your library. Governmental safety management system models tend to be more regulation based but still use variations of the core elements previously discussed for program administration. Refer to Appendix 6.3 for a Brief Summary Comparison of Governmental-Related Safety Management Systems Process Elements as follows: Table 6.6 Various Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Safety or Federal Voluntary Practices, Table 6.7 Selected Providence or International Standards, Table 6.8 OSHA’s Process Safety Management (PSM) and EPA Chemical Risk Management Program (RMP) Comparison Every effort has been made to provide a summary of various regulation, and Table 6.9 History of Older Standards for a Proposed Safety Management Programs. All Regulations are subject to change. The information presented is based on current standard. Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) updated and published several Guidelines for Safety and Health Programs in 2017 which include the following:
* Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs General Industry
* Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs in Construction.
These Recommended Practices provide a step-by-step approach to implementing a basic safety management system using seven core elements as discussed in this book. Refer to Appendix 6.4 for these relevant public domain documents that can be downloaded and used for your library Voluntary Protection Program (VPP) VPP has been an effective program based on OSHA studies in establishing in-depth compliance-based programs. As its title implies, the VPP is a voluntary effort, and its general acceptance remains limited to approximately 2200 nationwide participants. The Voluntary Protection Programs (VPP) promote effective worksite-based safety and health. In the VPP, management, labor, and OSHA establish cooperative relationships at workplaces that have implemented a comprehensive safety and health management system. Approval into VPP is OSHA’s official recognition of the outstanding efforts of employers and employees who have achieved exemplary occupational safety and health. The legislative underpinning for VPP is Section (2)(b)(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, which declares the Congress’s intent "to assure so far as possible every working man and woman in the Nation safe and healthful working conditions and to preserve our human resources - (1) by encouraging employers and employees in their efforts to reduce the number of occupational safety and health hazards at their places of employment, and to stimulate employers and employees to institute new and to perfect existing programs for providing safe and healthful working conditions. Statistical evidence for VPP’s success is impressive. The average VPP worksite has a Days Away Restricted or Transferred (DART) case rate of 52% below the average for its industry. These sites typically do not start out with such low rates. Reductions in injuries and illnesses begin when the site commits to the VPP approach to safety and health management and the challenging VPP application process. All About VPP (n.d.), Voluntary Protection Protection (VPP) (2016) If an organization is small or not ready to implement a robust safety management system, the VPP can be a good starting point and a worthwhile program to follow if its limitations are understood as noted. The VPP program success is based on injury rate reduction and compliance-based efforts. The effort required does not imply a safety culture has been developed within organizations using the program. The measurement of “downstream” may or may not be indicators that risk reduction has been improved. Department of Energy VPP Elements The Department of Energy Voluntary Protection Program (DOE-VPP) promotes safety and health excellence through cooperative efforts among labor, management, and government at the Department of Energy (DOE) contractor sites. DOE has also formed partnerships with other Federal agencies and the private sector for both advancing and sharing its Voluntary Protection Program (VPP) experiences and preparing for program challenges in the next century. The safety and health of contractor and federal employees are a high priority for the Department. 안전보건경영시스템의 단점 및 한계는 지속적인 프로세스가 유지되어야 하고 끊임없이 모니터링되어야 한다는 점이다. 다음과 같은 경우 안전보건경영시스템에 문제가 발생할 수 있다:
* 적절하게 실행되지 않아 다른 경영 프로세스와 통합되지 못한 "박제된/판에 박힌(canned)" 접근법으로 비춰질 때, 즉 표방된 가치(espoused values)만 제공할 뿐 조직을 실질적으로 이끌지 못할 때 발생한다.
* 그 적용 범위가 지나치게 협소하여 상호 연결된 총체적(holistic) 프로세스가 아닌 일련의 일회성 단편 프로그램으로 인식될 때이다.
* 활동과 프로세스에 대한 측정이 양심적이고 일관되게 수행되지 않으면 거짓된 안전 의식(false sense of safety)이 형성될 수 있다. 서류상으로만 완료 처리하는 "연필 굴리기(pencil whipping)"나 허위 문서화가 발생하지 않도록 정직하고 포괄적이며 일상적인 평가 시스템이 갖추어져야 한다.
* 부적절한 안전 행동이나 안전 프로세스의 미준수에 대해 징계나 제재와 같은 부정적 결과(consequences)가 일관되게 적용되지 않거나, 그와 반대로 안전 수칙 준수 및 모범 사례에 대한 긍정적 인정(positive recognition)이 결여되어 있을 때 시스템은 형해화된다.
* 경영진의 관심과 자원 투입이 일시적인 유행(fad)처럼 지나가고 지속적인 헌신으로 이어지지 못할 때 직원들은 냉소주의(cynicism)에 빠지게 된다.
* 시스템이 지나치게 관료화되고 복잡한 서류 작업에 치중하여 현장 작업자의 실질적인 안전 개선 활동을 저해하고 서류 작성만을 위한 업무 부담으로 전락할 때 실패한다.

이러한 단점과 함정을 극복하기 위해서는 경영시스템의 본질이 형식적인 문서화가 아니라 현장의 유해·위험요인을 실질적으로 제거하고 지속적인 개선(continuous improvement)을 달성하는 데 있음을 명확히 인식해야 한다. 미국 에너지부(DOE)와 민간 부문은 다음 세기의 프로그램 과제에 대비하고 자율안전보건프로그램(VPP) 경험을 공유하고 발전시키기 위해 긴밀히 협력해 왔다. 계약업체 직원과 연방 직원의 안전과 보건은 부서의 최우선 순위이다(DOE VPP 일반 정보, n.d.; 자율안전보건프로그램 DOE-VPP, 2016; 작업자 보건안전, n.d.).

(VPPPA) - The Premier Global Safety and Health Organization , is the leading organization dedicated to cooperative occupational safety, health and environmental management systems. VPPPA, a nonprofit 501 (c)(3) charitable organization, is a member-based association, providing a network of more than 2,300 companies and worksites who have achieved or are striving for occupational safety and health excellence, including the Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s (OSHA) or the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Voluntary Protection Programs (VPP). Voluntary protection program (DOE-VPP), (2016) The U.S. Department of Energy developed a comprehensive two-volume manual entitled, “Human Performance Improvement Handbook” (2009) while not a safety management system the manuals offer a wide array of concepts and criteria used in developing safety management systems. These concepts and criteria contained in the manuals provide an understanding of the underlying causes of human error and obstacles to developing a safety management culture. Human performance improvement (HPI) as addressed in this handbook is not a program per se, such as Six Sigma, Total Quality Management, and the like. Rather, it is a set of concepts and principles associated with a performance model that illustrates the organizational context of human performance. The model contends that human performance is a system that comprises a network of elements that work together to produce repeatable outcomes. The system encompasses organizational factors, job-site conditions, individual behavior, and results. The system approach puts a new perspective on human error: it is not a cause of failure, alone, but rather the effect or symptom of deeper trouble in the system. Human error is not random; it is systematically connected to features of people’s tools, the tasks they perform, and the operating environment in which they work. Human performance tools for individuals, work teams, and management, human performance improvement handbook (2009)

The Why 5 Technique Asking Five Why’s is a powerful tool that can be used to help identify and understand the root causes of defects in a process and to highlight incorrect assumptions about causes. By asking, “Why?” repeatedly allows one to peel back element to find symptoms of the system that cause specific issues. This technique also helps to identify how different causes of a problem may be related (Hafey, 2009). The following are some key concepts
* Describe the problem in specific terms.
* Ask why it happens.
* If the answer does not identify a root cause, ask why again.
Points to remember:
* Only operate on the fact—no hearsay.
* Focus on the process/aspects of a problem, rather than on the personalities involved. Finding scapegoats does not solve
problems!
* Answers to each successive “why” may require gathering.

The 5S fosters a culture of continuous improvement and employee engagement that is essential for successful implementation of any process (The lean and environment toolkit, 2007). Some organization has added a 6th component to the 5S concept, “Safety” (The lean and environment toolkit, 2007). Gap Analysis A gap analysis is a technique that enables an organization to identify the gap between the current state and the desired state to be achieved (Gap analysis, reaching your ideal future state, n.d.; Werde, 2015). A gap analysis consists of
* Listing of characteristic factors (such as attributes, competencies, performance levels) of the present situation (“what
is”)
* Listing factors needed to achieve future objectives (“what should be”)
* Highlighting the gaps that exist and need to be corrected (Gap analysis, 2018).

Histograms help provided an estimate as to where values are concentrated, what the extremes are, and whether there are any gaps (U.S. Coast Guard Leadership Development Center, 2014). ### Elements of Delegation
Delegation is a critical leadership method and involves more than just “passing the buck” to subordinates, telling them to “do what you need to do.” Leadership is still responsible for the results and cannot blame the subordinate if things go wrong. Leadership must be involved in periodic reports, performance reviews, and face-to-face discussions to assess the status of what has been delegated. Network analysis can be used to determine where and how responsibilities are shifted by assigned accountabilities and authorities. The network review can identify the location of assigned responsibilities and their impact on other personnel within the network as activities cascade through an organization. Refer Chapter 3, Analyzing and using Your Network. The man who grasps principals can successfully select his own methods. The man who tries methods, ignoring principles, is sure to have trouble. Ralph Waldo Emerson A triad of responsibility, authority, and accountability cannot be separated, and their impact must be considered as interrelated and together as a whole. The following discussion defines the triad and their importance:
* Is it the responsibility the duty of the person to complete the task assigned? A person who is given the responsibility
should ensure that tasks assigned are accomplished. If the tasks are not completed, then the individual should not give explanations or excuses. Responsibility without adequate authority leads to discontent and dissatisfaction. Responsibility flows from bottom to top. The middle level and lower level management hold more responsibilities than the upper level. The person held responsible for a job is answerable for it. If the person performs the tasks assigned as expected, there is need for praise. While if the person does not accomplish tasks assigned as expected, then also there needs to be an appropriate answer to why it was not accomplished (Delegation of Authority, 2018).
* Authority. In the context of a business organization, the term authority can be defined as the power and right of a person
to use and allocate the resources efficiently, to take decisions and to give orders to achieve the organizational objectives. Authority must be well defined. All individuals who have the authority should know what the scope of their authority is and they should not misuse it. Authority is the right to give commands, orders, and get the things done. Authority always flows from top to bottom where the top-level management has the greatest authority. It explains how a supervisors gets work done from their subordinate by clearly explaining what is expected and how it should be accomplished. Authority should be accompanied by an equal amount of responsibility. “Delegating the authority to someone else does not imply escaping from accountability. Accountability still rests with the person having the absolute authority”. (Delegation of Authority, 2018)
* Accountability means giving explanations for any variance in the actual performance from the expectations set.
Accountability cannot be delegated. For example, if ‘A’ is given a task with sufficient authority, and ‘A’ delegates this task to B and asks them to ensure that the task is done well, responsibility rest with ‘B,’ but accountability still rest with ‘A.’ The top-level management is most accountable. Accountability, in short, means being answerable for the result. Accountability cannot be escaped. It arises from responsibility (Accountability, 2017).
* Often, the word responsibility is used in conjunction with the word accountability. When hearing the word accountability, many people immediately equate it with responsibility and see the two as being the same (The
Performance-Based Management Handbook, Volume 3, Establishing Accountability for Performance, 2017).
* Assignment of Duties. The delegator first tries to define the task and duties to the subordinate. The task also must define
the result expected from the subordinates. Clarity of duty as expected has to be the first step in the delegation (Delegation of Authority, 2018).
* Granting of authority. Subdivision of authority takes place when a supervisor divides and shares authority with the
subordinate. It is for this reason every subordinate should be given enough independence to carry out the task as assigned. The managers at all levels delegate authority and power which is attached to their job positions. The subdivision of powers is significant to obtain effective results (Delegation of Authority, 2018).
* Creating Responsibility and Accountability. The delegation process does not end once powers are granted to the subordinates. They at the same time have to be obligatory toward the duties assigned to them. Responsibility is fundamental
as it gives power to authority. At the same time, responsibility is absolute and cannot be shifted. Accountability, on the other hand, is the obligation of the individual to carry out specific duties as per the standards of performance. Authority is delegated, responsibility is created, and accountability is imposed. Accountability arises out of responsibility and responsibility arises out of authority.
* Every manager, that is, the delegator, has to follow a system to finish up the delegation process. Equally important is the
delegate’s role which means the responsibility and accountability are attached to the authority (Delegation of Authority, 2018).

### 위임의 핵심 요소 (Elements of Delegation)

'위임(Delegation)'은 리더십의 결정적인 핵심 방법론이며, 부하 직원에게 “알아서 네가 해야 할 일을 하라”며 책임을 전가하고 발을 빼는 '책임 떠넘기기(Passing the buck)'가 결코 아닙니다. 리더는 최종 결과에 대해 여전히 전적인 책임을 져야 하며, 일이 잘못되었을 때 결코 부하 직원을 희생양 삼아 비난할 수 없습니다.

리더는 위임한 과업의 진행 상태를 객관적으로 파악하기 위해 정기 보고를 챙기고, 성과 검토를 진행하며, 대면 대화에 지속적으로 관여해야 합니다. 제3장(네트워크 분석 및 활용)에서 다루었던 조직 네트워크 분석(ONA)을 적용하면, 공식 부여된 책무성과 권한에 따라 책임이 사내에서 어디로 어떻게 이동하고 있는지를 한눈에 파악할 수 있습니다. 네트워크 검토는 안전 활동이 조직 전체로 파급되어 내려갈 때 배정된 책임의 실제 위치와 그것이 네트워크 내 다른 구성원들에게 미치는 상호 영향을 명확히 추적해 줍니다.

> "원리(Principles)를 꿰뚫고 있는 사람은 자신만의 독창적인 방법(Methods)을 성공적으로 선택할 수 있다. 그러나 원리를 무시한 채 오직 기교와 방법에만 매달리는 사람은 반드시 곤경에 처하게 된다."  
> — 랠프 월도 에머슨 (Ralph Waldo Emerson)

**책임(Responsibility), 권한(Authority), 책무성(Accountability)이라는 삼원조(Triad)**는 결코 개별적으로 분리될 수 없으며, 이들의 상호 영향력은 상호 연결된 하나의 완전한 전체로서 다루어져야 합니다. 다음의 논의는 이 삼원조의 본질과 중요성을 명확히 정의합니다:

* **책임(Responsibility)**이란 자신에게 부여된 과업을 성실히 완수해야 할 인간 본연의 의무를 의미합니다. 책임을 부여받은 사람은 자신에게 맡겨진 과업이 반드시 완수되도록 보장해야 합니다. 만약 과업이 완수되지 못했다면 구차한 변명이나 핑계를 대서는 안 됩니다. 적절한 권한이 수반되지 않은 일방적 책임 부과는 조직 구성원에게 깊은 불만과 좌절만을 안겨줍니다. 책임은 조직의 바닥에서부터 상부를 향해 상향식(Bottom to top)으로 흐릅니다. 중간 관리자와 일선 감독자는 최고경영진보다 더 많은 일상적 실천 책임을 직접 짊어집니다. 어떤 직무에 대해 책임을 진 사람은 그 일에 대해 공식적인 답변을 내놓아야 합니다(Answerable). 만약 기대한 대로 훌륭히 과업을 완수했다면 마땅히 칭찬과 보상이 뒤따라야 하며, 반대로 완수하지 못했다면 결함의 원인을 규명하고 시정 조치를 취해야 합니다.
* **권한(Authority)**이란 상급자가 부하 직원에게 합법적으로 명령을 내리고 조직의 자원을 통제할 수 있는 공식적인 법적·제도적 권리입니다. 권한은 상위 직위에서 하위 직위로 하향식(Top to bottom)으로 흐릅니다. 권한은 상급자로부터 하급자에게 성공적으로 위임될 수 있습니다.
* **책무성(Accountability)**이란 자신에게 맡겨진 직무의 최종 완수 여부에 대해 직속 상급자에게 공식 보고하고 결과를 해명해야 하는 절대적인 의무입니다. 책임은 타인에게 위임할 수 있지만, 책무성은 결코 타인에게 전가할 수 없는 절대적인 성격을 지닙니다.

## APPENDIX 7.2 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE LEADERSHIP TEAM

Top Leadership Team Members The leadership team establishes and provides the leadership, budget, and resources for carrying out the organization’s safety policy, goals, and objectives by.
* Establishing a policy to ensure that the organization stays in compliance with all applicable organizational, Best Management Practices, regulatory requirements, and so on
* Providing a safe work environment and working conditions for all employees
* Providing the leadership and resources to accomplish safety policies and procedures
* Resolving any conflicts of production priorities where safety is a concern
* Establishing the vision/mission, goals, and objectives
* Supporting the safety professional and employees in their requests for information, training, other professional services,
facilities, tools, and equipment needed to develop an effective safety process
* Assigning clear and understandable responsibilities for the various aspects of the safety process. Ensuring employees
with assigned responsibilities have adequate resources and authority to perform their assigned duties
* Hold managers, supervisors, and employees accountable for assigned responsibilities by checking to ensuring that they
are meeting their responsibilities and by recognizing them, as appropriate
* Evaluating the effectiveness of managers and supervisors regarding the safety process
* Keeping in touch with all employees, contractors, and so on, who perform safety activities
* Assisting in providing direction and authority for specific activities and visibly demonstrate involvement
* Setting an example by demonstrating commitment (following safety rules and safe work practices)
* Ensuring that all vendors, customers, contractors, and visitors comply with the company safety policy
* Thoroughly understand all hazards, potential hazards, and associated risk that employees may be exposed. Ensuring that
a comprehensive program of prevention and control is established and operating properly
* Providing a reliable system for employees to report hazardous conditions and other situations that appear hazardous.
Make sure that responses to employee’s reports are appropriate and timely
* Encouraging all employees to use established hazard reporting system(s).
* Establishing an inspection system, for example, self-inspections, and reviewing the results periodically to ensure that
proper and timely hazard correction are made
* Developing a preventive maintenance program to ensure that there is proper care and functioning of equipment and
facilities
* Reviewing loss-producing event reports to keep informed of causes and trends
* Providing medical and emergency response systems and first aid facilities adequate for the size and hazards at the
worksite
* Requiring periodic drills to make sure that each employee knows what to do in case of an emergency
* Developing training programs to help provide improvement and knowledge of all employees, managers, and supervisors. This training should help to recognize and understand hazards and to protect themselves and others.
(Managing worker safety and health, sample assignment of safety and health responsibilities, 2018; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013)

## 부록 7.2 최고경영진 리더십 팀의 안전 책임 표준 예시 (APPENDIX 7.2 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE LEADERSHIP TEAM)

최고경영진 리더십 팀 구성원은 다음의 활동을 통해 전사 안전보건 방침, 목표 및 세부 추진 과제를 완수하기 위한 확고한 리더십, 예산 및 자원을 솔선하여 확립하고 제공해야 합니다:
* 조직이 적용 가능한 모든 사내 규정, 업계 모범 경영 실무(BMP), 정부 규제 법규 요구사항을 완벽히 준수하도록 보장하는 공식 안전보건 방침을 수립한다.
* 전 임직원을 위해 안전하고 쾌적한 작업 환경과 물리적 작업 조건을 제공한다.
* 안전 방침과 절차를 현장에서 완벽히 실현할 수 있도록 필요한 리더십과 충분한 자원을 배정한다.
* 생산 납기 우선순위와 안전이 충돌하는 모든 상황에서, 안전을 최우선으로 하여 갈등을 단호하게 해결한다.
* 명확한 전사적 안전 비전, 사명(미션), 연간 목표 및 세부 추진 과제를 확립한다.
* 효과적인 안전 프로세스를 개발하는 데 필요한 정보, 교육훈련, 외부 전문 서비스, 시설 개선, 공구 및 안전 장비 요청에 대해 안전 전문가와 현장 직원들의 요구를 적극 지원한다.
* 안전 프로세스의 다양한 영역에 걸쳐 명확하고 이해하기 쉬운 구체적 책임을 배정한다. 책임을 부여받은 직원이 직무를 완수할 수 있도록 충분한 자원과 실질적 권한을 반드시 함께 부여한다.
* 부서장, 현장 감독자, 근로자가 부여받은 안전 책임을 다하고 있는지를 상시 점검하고, 탁월한 성과를 보인 자를 적절히 포상하고 인정함으로써 확고한 책무성을 집행한다.
* 안전 프로세스 실행에 관한 관리자와 감독자의 유효성을 정기적으로 공정하게 평가한다.
* 안전 활동을 수행하는 모든 임직원, 사내 도급 협력업체 인력들과 상시 긴밀한 접촉과 소통을 유지한다.
* 특정 안전 활동에 대한 명확한 방향성과 권한을 부여하고, 현장 활동에 눈에 보이게 직접 참여함으로써 솔선수범을 과시한다.
* 스스로 안전 규칙과 안전 작업 절차를 철저히 준수함으로써 전사적인 모범을 보인다.
* 모든 자재 공급업체, 고객, 도급업체 및 외부 방문객이 회사의 안전 방침을 철저히 준수하도록 보장한다.
* 직원들이 노출될 수 있는 모든 잠재적 유해위험요인과 관련 위험성을 철저히 파악하고, 포괄적인 예방 및 통제 프로그램이 수립되어 현장에서 완벽히 작동하도록 보장한다.
* 근로자가 현장의 위험한 상태나 의심스러운 상황을 불이익 없이 즉시 보고할 수 있는 신뢰성 있는 위험 보고 시스템을 제공하며, 접수된 보고에 대해 시의적절하고 적절한 조치를 취한다.
* 모든 직원이 전사 안전문화 발전에 적극적으로 참여하도록 강력히 장려한다.

## APPENDIX 7.3 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES PLANT/SITE SUPERINTENDENTS/MANAGERS

Managers help to maintain safe working conditions in their respective area of responsibilities by
* Providing the leadership and appropriate direction essential to maintain the safety policy as the fundamental value in the
organization
* Holding all supervisors accountable for their assigned safety roles and responsibilities, including their responsibility to
ensure that employees under their direction comply with all safety policies, procedures, and rules
* Evaluating the safety performance of supervisors, taking into account indicators of good performance, for example:
safety activities leading to reducing loss-producing events, housekeeping, involvement in safety activities, a positive approach to safety problems and solutions, and a willingness to implement recommendations
* Insisting that a high level of housekeeping is maintained, safe working procedures are established, and employees
follow procedures and apply good judgment to the hazardous aspects of all tasks
* Participating in regular inspections to observe conditions and to communicate with employees. Provide positive reinforcement and instruction during inspections, and require the correction of any hazards
* Actively participating in and supporting employee involvement in safety activities
* Providing timely and the appropriate follow-up on recommendations made by employee or safety committees
* Ensuring that all new facilities, equipment, materials, and processes are reviewed for existing and potential hazards, and
associated risk.
* Ensure that JHAs are conducted periodically for all jobs, with emphasis on specific tasks, so those hazards can be identified and minimized or controlled
* Ensure that employees know about the management system and are encouraged to use the systems for reporting hazards
and making safety suggestions. Ensure that employees are protected from reprisal, their input is considered, and that their ideas are adopted when helpful and feasible
* Ensuring that corrective action plans are developed where hazards are identified or unsafe acts are observed
* Ensuring that all hazardous tasks are covered by specific safe work procedures or rules to minimize injury
* Providing safety equipment and protective devices, as appropriate, and make sure employees understand and how to use
the equipment properly
* Ensuring that any injured employee regardless of how minor, receive prompt, and appropriate medical treatment
* Ensuring that all incidents are promptly reported, thoroughly investigated, and documented, and that safety recognition
programs do not discourage reporting of incidents
* Staying on top of incident trends Taking proper corrective action, as appropriate, to reverse trends
* Ensuring that all employees are physically qualified to perform their assigned task
* Ensuring that all employees are trained and retrained, as applicable, to recognize and understand hazards and to follow
safe work procedures
* Ensuring that supervisors conduct periodic safety meetings to review and analyze the causes of incidents and to promote
free discussion of hazardous conditions and possible solutions
* Using the safety manager to help promote aggressive and effective safety programs
* Helping to develop and implement emergency procedures
* Participating in safety program evaluation
(Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013)

## 부록 7.3 공장장 및 부서장의 안전 책임 표준 예시 (APPENDIX 7.3 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES PLANT/SITE SUPERINTENDENTS/MANAGERS)

공장장, 현장 소장 및 부서장들은 자신이 관할하는 현장 책임 구역 내에서 다음 활동을 실천함으로써 안전한 작업 조건을 유지할 책임을 집니다:
* 모든 사업 운영의 가장 기본적이고 타협할 수 없는 핵심 가치로서 전사 안전 방침을 유지하는 데 필수적인 리더십과 올바른 방향성을 제공한다.
* 모든 임직원이 안전하고 쾌적한 환경에서 근무할 수 있도록 완벽한 작업 환경과 조건을 제공한다.
* 유해위험요인을 사전에 선제적으로 식별하고 제거하기 위한 정기적인 현장 순찰 점검을 직접 수행한다.
* 사업장 내 모든 유해위험요인과 불안전한 행동이 발견 즉시 통제되거나 제거되도록 신속한 시정 조치를 지휘한다.
* 생산 목표를 달성하는 과정에서 안전이 결코 타협되거나 뒷전으로 밀리지 않도록 철저히 통제한다.
* 일선 관리감독자가 현장 작업자들에게 올바른 안전 지시와 지도를 내릴 수 있도록 확고한 권한과 자원을 부여한다.
* 관리감독자 및 근로자가 안전 규정을 충실히 이행하고 있는지를 일상적으로 감독하고, 안전 성과를 공정하게 평가하여 책무성을 확립한다.
* 발생한 모든 사고와 아차사고에 대해 즉각적인 조사를 실시하도록 지시하고, 재발 방지 대책이 현장에 완벽히 적용되었는지를 직접 확인한다.
* 현장 근로자들의 안전 교육훈련 이수 실태를 정기적으로 점검하고 미이수자가 작업에 투입되지 않도록 엄격히 통제한다.
* 사내 안전보건위원회에 적극적으로 참석하여 현장의 위험 개선 안건을 신속히 의결하고 예산을 지원한다.
* 현장 순회 경영(MBWA)을 주기적으로 실천하여 일선 작업자들과 1:1 안전 대화를 나누고 고충을 직접 해결한다.
* 법적 규제 기준 및 기업 내부 안전 표준이 관할 사업장의 모든 공정에 100% 누락 없이 적용되도록 보장한다.

## APPENDIX 7.4 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES FOR SUPERVISION

Supervisors help to maintain safe working conditions in their respective area of responsibilities by demonstrating their commitment to safety efforts by:
* Being thorough and conscientious in following the safe work procedures and safety rules that apply. Practice what you
preach
* Evaluating employee performance, for example, safe behavior and work methods
* Encouraging and actively support employee participation. Provide positive reinforcement and recognition and/or group
performance
* Maintaining up-to-date knowledge and skills required to understand specific hazards, for example, improperly functioning tools and/or equipment
* Maintaining good housekeeping
* Ensuring that the preventive maintenance program is being followed and that any hazards found and tracked to
completion
* Conducting frequent inspections, using a checklist, to evaluate physical conditions
* Investigating loss-producing events thoroughly to determine root cause and how hazards can be minimized or controlled
* Holding employees accountable for their safety responsibilities and actions
* Consistently and fairly, enforcing safety rules and procedures
* Discouraging shortcuts
* Providing on-the-job training in safe work procedures and the use and maintenance of equipment
* Ensuring that each employee knows what to do in case of an emergency
* Refer to the leadership team any resource needs you cannot resolve
(Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013)

## 부록 7.4 일선 관리감독자의 안전 책임 표준 예시 (APPENDIX 7.4 SAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES FOR SUPERVISION)

현장 관리감독자(조장, 반장, 직장)는 자신이 담당하는 구체적인 작업 구역 내에서 다음의 행동을 실천함으로써 안전에 대한 헌신을 입증하고 안전한 작업 조건을 유지해야 합니다:
* 모든 안전 작업 절차와 안전 수칙을 스스로 철저하고 양심적으로 준수함으로써 모범을 보인다.
* 매일 작업을 시작하기 전에 작업 전 안전 회의(TBM)를 개최하여 당일 작업의 유해위험요인과 필수 안전 대책을 전 작업자에게 명확히 전달한다.
* 작업자들이 작업에 적합한 올바른 개인보호구(PPE)를 완벽하게 착용하고 있는지를 작업 착수 전 및 작업 중에 상시 확인한다.
* 작업에 투입되는 모든 기계, 설비, 공구 및 방호 장치가 정상적으로 작동하고 결함이 없는지를 사전 점검한다.
* 불안전한 행동이나 위험한 조건을 목격했을 때 즉시 작업을 중지시키고 올바른 안전 작업 방법을 코칭한다.
* 신규 배치 근로자나 전입 근로자에 대해 해당 공정의 직무 위험 분석(JHA) 내용을 상세히 교육하고 밀착 지도한다.
* 관할 구역 내에서 발생한 모든 부상, 사고, 아차사고 및 시설 파손을 관리자에게 즉시 보고하고 근본 원인 조사에 적극 참여한다.
* 작업자가 현장의 위험을 보고했을 때 이를 경청하고, 즉시 시정 조치하거나 자체 해결이 불가능할 경우 상급 관리자에게 지체 없이 에스컬레이션한다.
* 작업장 내 통로 구획, 5S 정리정돈 및 청결 상태를 상시 유지하여 전도 및 낙하 위험을 사전에 차단한다.

### Permanent Sub-Committees
A wide array of activities can be taken on by the central committee. To reduce the time requirements and demands on the members, various tasks can be delegated to members who in turn lead and manage the specific subcommittee. These subcommittees coordinate and share their information to provide overall consistency and ensure that no gaps between the subcommittees develop. Permanent Sub-Committees could include, but are not limited to, the following:
* Publicity.
* Inspections and Walk-Throughs.
* Incident Reports.
* Job Hazard Analysis.
* Rules, Procedures, and Standards.
* Education and Training.
* Housekeeping.
* Follow-up.

### 영구 분과위원회 (Permanent Sub-Committees)

중앙 안전위원회 하나만으로 방대한 전사 안전 활동 전체를 모두 직접 도맡아 처리하는 것은 불가능합니다. 중앙 위원들의 과도한 시간적 부담과 피로를 덜어주기 위해, 구체적인 안전 과업들을 세부 분과위원회로 분산 위임하고 각 분과위원회를 전담 위원들이 책임지고 이끌도록 구조화해야 합니다.

각 분과위원회는 상호 긴밀한 정보 공유와 조율을 통해 전사적 일관성을 유지하며, 분과 간에 어떠한 안전 공백도 발생하지 않도록 긴밀히 협력합니다. 상설 운영되는 영구 분과위원회에는 다음의 핵심 분과들이 포함될 수 있습니다:
1. 안전 홍보 분과위원회 (Publicity)

4. 직무 위험 분석 분과위원회 (Job Hazard Analysis - JHA)

8. 개선 후속 조치 분과위원회 (Follow-up)

If no agreement can be reached between the supervisor and the employee, then the concerns will be discussed with the next level of leadership. This discussion will include the employee, the employee’s direct leader and the next level of leadership, and so on, and discussion continues until an agreement is reached between all parties. This process must continue until everyone involved is in agreement as to the level of risk and potential outcome. This perceived risk rating is discussed in detail with a member of the leadership team during which the employee will share their concerns. Both the leadership team member and employee must mutually agree with the analysis before the task can be continued. The risk assessment discussion moves to the next level of leadership If:
* The supervisor and employee cannot agree on the risk rating and a solution. The supervisor cannot order the task to proceed

* A risk rating 3 has conditions or is a situation that cannot be resolved at this level of the organization.
An objective of the risk guidance card is to develop situational awareness of the potential for a loss-producing event. * Green indicates errors may occur, but errors will be caught by the individual.
* Yellow indicates the potential for errors has increased.

## OVERALL RISK MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
Effective risk management specifies and defines the levels of responsibility and authority of the leadership team and may include the following:
* Defining what is an unacceptable risk and ensuring a full understanding of the potential negative impact of risk
assessed.
* Assessing risks, developing risk reduction alternatives, and defining residual risk concerns and issues.
* Identifying unnecessary or ineffective risk controls for modification or replacement.
* Selecting risk reduction options from recommendations based on risk assessment.
* Accepting or rejecting risk based on its potential severity and predetermined risk tolerance.
* Training and educating employees on the selected risk management tools and techniques. Refer Chapter 11, Developing
Safety Training Needs.
* Ensuring that risk is only taken at the appropriate organizational level, and as needed, elevating risk decisions to a higher
leadership level, that is, the organization is not exposed to a high risk based on decisions made at a low level of management. This shift implies the next higher level of leadership has a full understanding of any associated risk and its control status.
* Integrating risk assessment methods into the business planning process to ensure that time and money are budgeted for
implementation of necessary controls (Carter & Smith, 2001; Occupational Health & Safety Management Systems, 2012; Risk management toolkit, 2018).

## 전사적 위험관리 책임 (OVERALL RISK MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES)

실효성 있는 위험관리는 경영진 리더십 팀의 책임과 권한의 한계를 명확히 규정하며, 다음의 핵심 책무들을 포함합니다:
* 무엇이 우리 조직에서 결코 용인될 수 없는 '수용 불가능한 위험(Unacceptable risk)'인지를 엄격히 정의하고, 평가된 위험이 초래할 잠재적 파괴 충격에 대해 전사적인 깊은 이해를 확립한다.
* 사업장 내 모든 위험을 과학적으로 평가하고, 위험을 줄이기 위한 다각적인 대체 대책을 개발하며, 최종적으로 남게 되는 잔여 위험(Residual risk)을 지속 추적한다.
* 현장에서 불필요하거나 비효과적인 것으로 판명된 낡은 안전 통제 규정을 과감히 식별하여 수정하거나 정예화된 새로운 절차로 대체한다.
* 잠재적 손실 사건과 관련된 아차사고 및 위험 제안 데이터를 체계적으로 수집, 분석 및 문서화한다.
* 조직의 모든 계층에 걸쳐 개방적이고 투명한 위험 소통이 자유롭게 흐르도록 보장한다.
* 위험성평가와 직무 위험 분석(JHA)을 완성하는 데 필요한 충분한 예산, 인력 및 전문 자원을 차질 없이 배정한다.

## ABSS SYSTEM AND THE BASIC ELEMENTS

Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts.
Albert Einstein The elements of an ABSS system can be used to move past the scripted approach, allowing supervision to start using their personalized approach and creativity. The ABSS consist of the following elements:
* Employee meetings that consist of the following:
* Daily preshift reviews
* Weekly meetings
* Monthly meeting
* One-on-one discussions with individual employees.
* Area walk-through tours, housekeeping, hazard identification, life safety, and so on.
* Machine/equipment specific checklists.
* Follow-up teams.
* Performance metrics. Refer Appendix 11.2, for an example list of ABSS Duties, and responsibilities. Refer Appendix 11.3 an example of suggested ABSS metrics.

## ABSS 시스템과 4대 기본 구성요소 (ABSS SYSTEM AND THE BASIC ELEMENTS)

ABSS를 지탱하는 핵심 기본 구성요소는 다음의 4가지 축으로 정립된다:
1. **계층별 안전 회의 (Safety Meetings)**: 일일 교대 전 검토(Daily Preshift Review), 주간 안전 회의(Weekly Meetings), 월간 종합 회의(Monthly Meetings)로 이어지는 위계적이고 체계적인 소통 회의 체계.
2. **근로자와의 1:1 심층 대화 (One-on-One Discussions with Employees)**: 관리감독자가 근로자와 정기적으로 마주앉아 위험 지각과 안전 고충을 경청하는 신뢰 구축 면담.
3. **현장 안전 순회 점검 (Safety Walk-Through Tour)**: 형식적인 적발 감사가 아니라, 현장의 잠재 위험을 함께 찾아내고 소통하는 능동적 관찰 투어.
4. **기계·설비 맞춤형 점검표 및 사후조치 팀 (Machine/Equipment-Specific Checklist & Follow-up Team)**: 작업자가 가동 전 결함을 즉각 포착하는 세부 체크리스트와, 접수된 안전 작업 요청서를 신속하고 공정하게 해결하는 노사 합동 사후조치 전담반.

## SAFETY MEETINGS

For an organization to be successful in sustaining a safety culture, all areas of the organization should conduct specific types of safety training or coaching meetings. The perception of safety meetings and information applies to “others but not me,” should be removed. A safety culture provides a clear message for communicating to all employees that they have a defined role to play in the safety management system. All employees should understand the requirements and importance of safetyrelated issues in their organization.

An organization is essentially a network of individuals as graphically shown in organizational charts. Refer Chapter 3, Analyzing and Using Your Network, Fig. 3.1, for an Example Organizational Chart. Each work team or area of responsibility is more than just a box on an organizational chart. It is a network of individuals influenced by person-to-person and face-to-face communications that can be influenced by the behavior and communications of everyone in the organization. Refer Chapter 3, Analyzing and Using Your Network, Fig. 3.4 for an example of how the Lines of Connection from Six People or Nodes Potential affect the process.

The nature of any organization is complex and how information is moved through all levels of the organization is critical to the safety management system. The “Day-to-day feedback is important to ensure improved leader…performance” (Leadership development, field manual, 6-22, 2015) and provides insights into corrective actions necessary to reach its goals and objectives. 

> **Three Degrees of Influence Rule** (Christakis & Fowler, 2009):  
> *"Everything we do or say ripples through our network, having an impact on our friends (one degree), our friend’s friend (two degrees) and the friend’s friend’s friend (three degrees). This rule applies to a broad range of attitudes, feelings, and behaviors."*

 Safety meetings can be used to affect the “three degrees of influence”. Based on the need to expand influence, three types of meetings, as discussed have been found to be the most efficient, daily preshift reviews, weekly meetings, and monthly meetings. These meetings range from a free-form format to an agenda-driven meeting used to communicate specific safety-specific information directly with each workgroup.

The following discussion will provide an approach to why shift meetings are determined to be successful. Variations can be used to adjust to the working requirements and employee availability. The intent is to embed safety communication into the work environment using a tiered series of meetings to keep a high level of communication in place.

## 안전 회의 체계 (SAFETY MEETINGS)

안전 회의는 네트워크 이론에서 강조하는 "3단계 영향력 법칙(three degrees of influence)"을 현장에 실질적으로 관철시키는 가장 강력한 도구이다. 조직 내 영향력을 빈틈없이 확장하기 위해, 앞서 언급한 일일 교대 전 검토, 주간 회의, 월간 회의의 3가지 회의 유형이 가장 효율적인 방식으로 입증되었다. 이러한 회의들은 자유로운 토론 형태(free-form format)부터 구체적인 안전 의제에 기반한 공식 회의에 이르기까지 다양하게 구성되어 각 작업 그룹과 직접 소통하는 데 사용된다.

다음의 논의는 왜 이러한 정기 교대 회의들이 성공적인 것으로 입증되었는지에 대한 핵심 접근법을 제공할 것이다. 작업 현장의 구체적 여건과 근로자들의 근무 교대 일정에 맞추어 유연한 변형이 적용될 수 있다. 본질적인 핵심 의도는 일련의 다층적 회의 체계를 통해 일터 환경 깊숙이 안전 소통을 단단히 내재화함으로써 고도의 활발한 소통 수준을 상시 유지하는 데 있다.

---

issues.en:
### ONE-ON-ONE DISCUSSIONS WITH EMPLOYEES

One-on-one discussions are not intended to trigger an adverse reaction or response from the supervisor. One-on-one talks are routine short discussions centered on safety concerns. These one-on-one discussions should not be held in the supervisor’s office where the employee may perceive the situation as awkward or intimidating. Such discussions should be conducted in the employee’s work environment where the employee may be more comfortable.

The “one-on-one discussion” is used as a direct face-to-face discussion with real-time feedback between the supervisor and each employee in the organization. The idea is to bypass group situations where employees will not speak up in meetings due to shyness, fear, mistrust, or other reasoning. By using a direct one-to-one approach, employees can privately discuss with their supervisor, the concerns about the information provided in the safety meetings that they would not bring up in front of their peers.

Supervision and employees can easily drift into an adversarial mode as traditional safety-related efforts typically only look for employee errors, production, or service-related issues. Given the hierarchy and structures of organizations, supervision may believe requesting or asking for employee feedback is a threat to their authority. This is the reason that the faceto-face, one-on-one meeting is important. According to George Robotham (as cited in Health and Safety Risk Management) “Research by Harvard professor T.J. Larkin suggests when communicating change with the workforce use the supervisor, not senior management, use face to face communications and frame communications relevant to the immediate work area and processes” (Robotham, 2014).
issues.ko:
### 근로자와의 1:1 심층 대화 (ONE-ON-ONE DISCUSSIONS WITH EMPLOYEES)

관리감독자와 현장 근로자 사이에 정기적으로 이루어지는 1:1 대화(One-on-One Discussions)는 안전문화를 혁신하는 데 있어 가장 강력하면서도 가장 간과되기 쉬운 핵심 활동이다. 대규모 회의에서는 동료들의 시선이나 조직적 위계로 인해 차마 입 밖으로 꺼내지 못했던 미묘한 위험 인식, 직무 스트레스, 장비 조작의 어려움, 안전 규칙 준수를 가로막는 실질적인 현장 압박 등이 바로 이 비공식적이고 친밀한 1:1 대화를 통해 비로소 수면 위로 솔직하게 드러나기 때문이다.

이러한 1:1 대화는 관리감독자가 근로자를 감시하거나 문책하기 위한 자리가 결코 아니다. 이는 근로자가 작업 현장에서 겪고 있는 실질적인 안전 고충과 위험 지각을 진심으로 경청하고, 상호 간의 인간적 신뢰와 심리적 안전감(psychological safety)을 견고하게 구축하기 위한 적극적인 소통의 장이다. 정기적인 1:1 대화를 통해 관리감독자는 현장 작업의 숨겨진 잠재 위험을 조기에 포착할 수 있으며, 근로자는 자신이 조직으로부터 진정으로 보호받고 존중받고 있다는 강력한 정서적 유대감을 형성하게 된다.

---

issues.en:
### SAFETY WALK-THROUGH TOUR

Safety inspections, observations, and walk-throughs are a core feature of safety management system elements. Unfortunately, walk-through tours can evolve or be perceived as a negative with fault-finding activities becoming adversarial between the leadership team and employees. Worksite inspections have been stressed as a core element of leadership since its beginning. Peters and Waterman updated the concept in their classic “In Search of Excellence,” as “management by wandering around” (Peters & Waterman, 2004). They stressed management should routinely get away from their office and desks and walk around reconnecting with the workplace. There comes a time when what is needed is not just rhetoric, but boots on the ground.
Baldwin Spencer The safety walk-through is an essential component of ABSS and is conducted as a joint effort by a diverse team consisting of supervision, a member of the leadership team, and employees as applicable.

The objective is to have a group that brings a variety of perceptions, backgrounds, expertise, and different points of view on the work environment. The participation of a member of the leadership team is to provide authority and awareness providing a presence to all employees that this effort is considered important and valuable to the organization.

By varying the time of the safety walk-through, the group can meet and talk to different employees and see the work environment under different conditions. In multishift or 7/24 operations, make sure all shifts have a walk-through as necessary.

The safety walk-through is completed during the typical workday or shift, once per month, and at the designated time built into the organizations planning function.

The safety walk-through should last no more than one hour in length and is not to be treated as a formal inspection. Rather, it is used as an awareness and observation activity allowing the group to interact with employees to identify concerns regarding hazards.

After this walk-through, any safety issues noted will require a risk assessment and a safety work order, assigned task, created for these issues to be resolved.
issues.ko:
### 현장 안전 순회 점검 (SAFETY WALK-THROUGH TOUR)

현장 안전 순회 점검(Safety Walk-Through Tour)은 관리감독자와 리더십 팀이 직접 생산 현장을 발로 누비며 작업 환경의 물리적 상태와 근로자들의 작업 행동을 체계적으로 관찰하는 핵심 활동이다. 여기서 절대 주의해야 할 점은, 이 순회 점검이 과거의 경찰관식 '적발 및 처벌 감사(gotcha audit)'로 변질되어서는 결코 안 된다는 점이다.

진정한 안전 순회 점검의 목적은 현장의 근로자들과 현장에서 직접 눈을 맞추며, 작업 중 위험하거나 불편한 점은 없는지 질문하고, 안전하게 작업을 수행하고 있는 긍정적인 행동에 대해 즉각적인 칭찬과 인정을 제공하는 데 있다. 리더가 현장을 정기적으로 순회하며 안전에 진심으로 관심을 기울이는 모습을 보여줄 때, 현장에는 "우리의 리더들은 안전을 무엇보다 중요하게 생각한다"는 강력한 가시적 신호(visible signal)가 전파된다.

issues.en:
### OBSERVATION 2

The machine specific checklist was developed after a major incident was uncovered during an operation’s inspection program. In the paper process, a load turner is used to rotate a 6-foot stack of paper. The base consists of a 300-pound plate held in place by bolts. An incident occurred when the plate was in a raised position. Several bolts broke, weakening other bolts, causing the heavy plate to fall. After the incident investigation, a machine/equipment checklist was put in place to review the bolts in the unit to ensure that none were broken or missing. The initial list was developed through employee discussions which uncovered previously unknown hazards. Upon review of other similar equipment, further concerns were found. A machine equipment-specific checklist was developed for each piece of equipment, to reduce the potential for recurrence. Creating these checklists was a coordinated effort between the safety staff, supervisors, and employees.

This checklist was expanded to all types of equipment in each facility. The idea of this checklist is that each piece of equipment is checked each day, before starting operation and documented as to the results observed.

The checklist is not static and is considered a living document, as additional hazards are observed. The checklist is not intended to be a maintenance checklist, as it is to be a quick reference to ensure that the primary hazards are reviewed and controlled before the daily activities begin.

To effectively use this checklist, employees on each shift will review the machine or equipment before production begins, rate each checklist item using the risk guidance card, as discussed in Chapter 9, Defining Risk Perception.
