### FIG. 11.3 Example operator general observations & machine/equipment-specific daily inspection checklist.

If the employee who reviews the checklist finds that an item is unacceptable, based on the risk guidance card, the supervisor is contacted, and a review is conducted by reviewing the machine or equipment.

Also, the completed checklist can be used as part of the one-on-one discussions with employees where the supervisor and employee will discuss elements on the list and validate the review is acceptable to both the employee and the supervisor. In reviewing the checklist as described before, and if there is a safety issue identified, an agreement needs to be reached between the employee and the supervisor as to the nature, type of the hazard, and the potential risk before the equipment can be put in operation.

As discussed in Chapter 9, Defining Risk Perception, if no agreement is reached, the next level of leadership is contacted and a second discussion begins. The intent of having these discussions is to reduce the potential and probability that employees will continue to operate machinery or equipment that is not functioning as intended and believing they have no alternative but to use the machinery or equipment in an unsafe condition.

An active safety culture reduces the acceptance of unnecessary risk, and the machine/equipment checklist provides an immediate discussion and correction.

issues.en:
## TRAINING IDEAS AND CREATIVE APPROACHES

As part of a Six Sigma Project, James managed a study to provide specific information concerning the improvement of the work environment. The study was conducted to assess the potential use of Six Sigma methods to evaluate how to improve the retention of safety information. A joint leadership and employee team was established to conduct the project using selected Six Sigma tools. At the time, the use of quality control-based methods was still not readily accepted or considered viable. The idea was to determine if employees, including leadership and supervision, were able to recall and discuss specific risk information as presented in the daily preshift review. The review sessions were followed up by one-on-one discussions held during the day that the information was presented, after one week, and one month. The retention rate was not what was expected. The project included determining ways to improve the learning retention rates of employees about hand safety.

Hand Safety related to this six sigma project will be discussed in more detailed in Chapter 12 Using the Job Hazard Analysis.

A limited Six Sigma tool, Gage Repeatability, and Reproducibility (R&R) study (Gage R&R, 2017) was conducted using supervisors and employees who knew the production process. The study was conducted to determine if excessive variability existed in the measurement system. In this project, it was used to assess the potential for the use of Six Sigma tools in determining the variability of training instructions and materials given to employees and how effectively the information was retained.

The study indicated a significant gap existed between what the supervisors believed was being communicated and the retention rate of employees remembering the various discussions. The bottom line was that the desired safety message was not getting through to employees. This was based on an interview with selected employees after preshift meetings.

Training ideas and creative approaches can be found being used in a range of venues. For example, during a safety committee brainstorming session searching for ideas on how to improve Shift-Review Retention Effectiveness, a member of the six sigma team brought up the concept of “Blues Clues?” Most members were not familiar with the concept. This member explained that his kids had learned some behaviors using the methods taught through repetition that was presented by the cartoon “Blues Clues.” As a team listened to this member’s discussion, it started to make some sense of how the process of retention could be improved.

---

> What is “Blues Clues?” "Blue’s Clues” is a cartoon series developed for children, ages 3 to 5 years. Where “…researchers found that preschoolers have a longer attention span and a stronger need to interact with characters than previous shows like Sesame Street had provided)” (Tracy, 2002). “Blue’s Clues for Success provides eight clues to achieving phenomenal success, for example,…Mobilize the energy in your organization by turning your MISSION into a ‘mantra’ ... and Consciously manage your CULTURE the way you manage every other aspect of your business” (Tracy, 2002). “Too many of us have allowed our ‘childlike’ values to be programmed right out of us-and. As a result, too many companies are failing to live up to their full potential” (Tracy, 2002). The comment presented a challenge to the team by asking the question: What If we encouraged everyone to keep an open mind and just think about how training was currently being presented and the consistency of its message. The question was expanded to What if we made safety training simple where immediate results could be observed. A great take away concept from “Blues Clues” included the following statement, “If companies could harness the imagination and creativity of the” child within “their people, they would have no competition” (Tracy, 2002). Adults have different behaviors than children, but the process of learning is the same. Of importance is the understanding that we cannot provide one orientation or one session and expect long-term retention of information. Training programs have long stressed the need for understanding the employee learning curve and how important knowledge is forgotten in a short period.

---

## 교육 훈련의 창의적 접근법과 아이디어 (TRAINING IDEAS AND CREATIVE APPROACHES)

식스 시그마(Six Sigma) 프로젝트의 일환으로, 제임스(James)는 작업 환경의 실질적인 개선에 관한 구체적인 정보를 도출하기 위한 심층 연구를 총괄 지휘하였다. 이 연구는 현장의 안전 정보 기억 및 파지율(retention of safety information)을 어떻게 향상시킬 수 있는지 평가하기 위해 식스 시그마 기법의 잠재적 활용 가능성을 측정하고자 수행되었다. 엄선된 식스 시그마 전문 도구들을 활용하여 프로젝트를 추진하기 위해 노사 합동의 리더십-근로자 태스크포스 팀이 구성되었다. 당시만 해도 품질 관리 기반의 방법론을 안전 분야에 적용하는 것은 결코 일반적이거나 쉽게 받아들여지지 않던 시절이었다. 연구의 핵심 착안점은 리더십과 관리감독자를 포함한 현장 근로자들이 일일 교대 전 검토에서 전달받은 구체적인 위험 정보들을 실제로 얼마나 정확하게 기억해내고 논의할 수 있는지를 과학적으로 규명하는 것이었다. 일일 교대 전 검토 세션이 끝난 직후, 정보가 전달된 당일, 1주일 후, 그리고 1개월 후에 각각 1:1 면담을 통해 추적 조사를 실시하였다. 그러나 충격적이게도 현장의 정보 기억 파지율은 당초 예상했던 수준에 턱없이 미치지 못했다. 이에 본 프로젝트는 특히 '손 안전(hand safety)'에 관한 근로자들의 학습 기억 파지율을 극대화할 수 있는 혁신적인 방안을 규명하는 연구를 본격적으로 포함하게 되었다.

식스 시그마 프로젝트와 관련된 손 안전의 상세 내용은 제12장 '직무위험성평가(JHA)의 활용'에서 더욱 깊이 있게 다룰 것이다.

생산 공정에 정통한 현장 관리감독자들과 근로자들을 대상으로 게이지 반복성 및 재현성(Gage R&R, Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility) 연구(Gage R&R, 2017)라는 특화된 식스 시그마 도구가 적용되었다. 이 연구는 측정 시스템 자체에 과도한 변동성(variability)이 존재하는지를 판별하기 위해 수행되었다. 본 프로젝트에서 게이지 R&R은 근로자들에게 제공되는 교육 훈련 지침과 교재의 변동성을 정밀하게 측정하고, 전달된 정보가 실질적으로 얼마나 효과적으로 근로자들의 뇌리에 유지·기억되는지를 평가하는 데 사용되었다.

연구 결과, 관리감독자들이 스스로 효과적으로 전달했다고 믿고 있는 내용과, 실제 근로자들이 회의 후 기억하고 있는 회상 파지율 사이에는 상상을 초월하는 거대한 간극(significant gap)이 존재한다는 사실이 명백히 드러났다. 요컨대 조직이 의도했던 핵심 안전 메시지가 현장 근로자들에게 사실상 전혀 도달하지 못하고 있었던 것이다. 이는 선발된 근로자들과의 심층 인터뷰를 통해 가감 없이 확인되었다.

## MEASURING THE ABSS PERFORMANCE

Safety performance and safety management system elements are of no benefit unless they are clearly and routinely communicated throughout the organization. 

> *"The majority of measures should be leading indicators that focus on proactive activities on the part of all employees—measures that track what people are doing daily to prevent accidents. With such measures in place, immediate and certain consequences can be engineered in to ensure those activities occur."*  
> — *(Judy Agnew & Aubrey Daniels, 2011)*

 

> *"It is often said that only those things that get measured, get done; and that, since only certain things can be measured, it is hardly a surprise when managers or organizations are assessed on short-term criteria."*  
> — *(Safety Culture in Nuclear Installations, 2002)*

 Various performance indicators can be used to measure the organization’s safety management system criteria. Specific assessments provide information on whether actions are being implemented as designed, assessing trends, or patterns related to those actions. Indicators provide information along with a time line of activities:
* Lagging. Measure outcomes after events have occurred. Loss-producing events are lagging indicators. Incident rates and loss analyses can provide trends and patterns of possible problems but do not necessarily predict future events or provide links to why events occur. They can be used to direct activities to areas of concern.
* Leading. Measures prevent conditions and activities which, if correctly implemented reduce the hazards and risks within an organization. The activities of the safety management system are leading indicators. Risk assessment is a type of leading indicator. These indicators are used to assess the potential of future performance and measure organizational “health” (Human performance tools for individuals, work teams, and management, 2009) Specific indicators offer insights on gaps in responsibility, for example, activities being skipped, thoroughness of reports, corrective actions effectiveness, and so on.

---

## ABSS 성과의 과학적 측정 (MEASURING THE ABSS PERFORMANCE)

안전 성과와 안전보건경영시스템의 핵심 요소들은 조직 전체에 걸쳐 명확하고 일상적으로 투명하게 소통되지 않는다면 아무런 실질적 유익을 가져다주지 못한다.

> "안전 측정 지표의 대부분은 모든 근로자가 자발적으로 수행하는 사전 예방적 활동에 초점을 맞추는 선행 지표(leading indicators)여야 한다. 즉, 사고를 사전에 예방하기 위해 사람들이 매일 무엇을 실천하고 있는지를 정밀하게 추적하는 지표여야 한다. 이러한 선행 지표 체계가 확립될 때, 그러한 안전 활동들이 현장에서 반드시 매일 실행되도록 보장하는 즉각적이고 확실한 긍정적 결과(consequences)를 시스템 내에 정밀하게 설계해 넣을 수 있다."  
> — 주디 애그뉴 & 오브리 대니얼스(Judy Agnew & Aubrey Daniels, 2011)

> "측정되는 것만이 실제로 실행된다는 말이 자주 회자된다. 그리고 오직 특정한 것들만이 측정될 수 있기 때문에, 경영자나 기업 조직이 당장 눈앞의 단기적 기준에 의해서만 평가받는 것은 결코 놀라운 일이 아니다."  
> — 《원자력 시설의 안전문화(Safety Culture in Nuclear Installations)》(2002)

조직의 안전보건경영시스템 기준을 정밀하게 측정하기 위해 다양한 성과 지표들이 폭넓게 활용될 수 있다. 특정한 세부 평가들은 프로세스가 계획대로 잘 가동되고 있는지, 아니면 치명적인 문제가 누적되고 있는지에 대한 생생한 실시간 정보를 제공해 준다.

## TOOLS THAT SUPPORT AND ADD VALUE TO THE SAFETY PROCESS

A six sigma project can take on a life of its own and lead the project manager in many directions, as was discussed, regarding the training retention rates. At each juncture of the project, the project manager needs to stop, think, and decide if the discussions through the brainstorming sessions offer a better alternative to enhance the safety process. The problem is that, for example, in the hand laceration project, as the team was brainstorming ideas, there were several directions that were discussed that could relate to the original intent. In this example, the project needed to be expanded to enhance the safety management system based on some gaps noted in the system such as:
* Improvement in the incident investigation guidelines.
* Development of an incident information management system to include a “Grab N Go Kit” of selected forms (Create a Grab n Go-Kit & Effectively Manage Incidents, 2018).
* Developing an ergonomics awareness checklist to aid in managing alleged reports of soft tissue.
* Identifying of the appropriate Glove and Knife equipment and updated procedures. The glove and knife and procedures will be discussed in detail in Chapter 12, Using the Job Hazard Analysis.

## 안전 프로세스를 지원하고 가치를 더하는 도구들 (TOOLS THAT SUPPORT AND ADD VALUE TO THE SAFETY PROCESS)

안전 프로세스를 실무에서 강력하게 뒷받침하고 부가가치를 창출하기 위해 다음과 같은 검증된 실무 지원 도구들이 유기적으로 결합되어 활용되어야 한다:
* 명문화된 사고 조사 가이드라인(Incident Investigation Guidelines).
* 통합 사고 정보 관리 시스템(Incident Information Management).
* 부상 관리 프로세스 표준 핸드북(Injury Management Process Booklet).
* 인체공학적 위험성 점검 키트 및 '그랩 앤 고(Grab N Go)' 현장 도구함.

이러한 도구들은 위기 상황이 닥쳤을 때 조직 구성원들이 우왕좌왕하지 않고 표준화된 프로토콜에 따라 차분하고 과학적으로 대처할 수 있도록 든든한 나침반 역할을 수행한다.

issues.en:
### INCIDENT INVESTIGATION GUIDELINES

Changes in the type and scope of operational risks can increase the potential for all types of incidents. An essential element of the safety management system is the effective administration of incident investigations and the development of an incident management process. An investigation process addresses weaknesses found in the safety process and determines the necessary controls and actions needed to reduce overall loss potential. Leadership should be provided with an understanding of what creates the conditions leading to loss-producing events to structure the formal reports required for operational, legal, regulatory, and insurance purposes.

The intent of this section is not to provide a comprehensive incident investigation procedure. Incident investigation is too complicated a topic to be fully covered in this section. The information presented, provides a brief framework for a basic incident investigation guideline with references selected to aid in developing or improving an investigative process to support a safety culture.

At its core, active investigations incorporate the use of a structured problem-solving format. The investigation process should be designed to include an objective evaluation of all available facts, opinions, statements, and related information, the identification of the root cause(s), including behaviors, and actions to be taken to help prevent recurrence.

The incident investigation subcommittee as discussed in Chapter 8, Getting Employees Involved in the Safety Management System, will help to guide the process and establishing criteria for its continued improvement. Use of the subcommittee and involvement of senior leadership can reduce the potential for an organization not taking recommended corrective actions seriously or corrective actions not being implemented promptly. The potential for failure to implement corrective actions is well documented. The investigation examples as we discussed previously in Chapter 2, Analyzing the Organizational Culture, the two NASA space shuttle losses noted safety culture and safety management system concerns which remained uncorrected.

The US Department of Energy (DOE) notes, “The best metaphor for how accidents are investigated is a simple maze. If a group of people is asked to solve the maze as quickly as possible and the ‘winners’ are asked how they did it, invariably the answer will be that they worked it from the Finish to the Start.” (Accident and operational safety analysis, volume I:
Accident analysis techniques, 2012) The DOE further notes that “Like a maze, accident investigations look backward. What was uncertain for the people working forward through the maze becomes clear for the investigator looking backward.” (Accident and operational safety analysis, volume I: Accident analysis techniques, 2012; Course 702, effective accident investigation, the basics, 2017; refer Fig. 11.7). Refer Appendix 11.8, for an example basic incident investigation guideline framework.

### 사고 조사 가이드라인 (INCIDENT INVESTIGATION GUIDELINES)

사고 조사의 궁극적인 목표는 결코 특정 개인의 잘못을 찾아내어 비난하거나 처벌하는 '문책 및 범인 색출(fault-finding)'이 되어서는 절대 안 된다. 진정한 조사의 목적은 사고를 유발한 시스템적 근본 원인(root cause)을 밝혀내어 향후 동일하거나 유사한 재발을 영구적으로 방지하는 '객관적 사실 규명(fact-finding)'에 확고히 초점을 맞추어야 한다.

사고 조사는 종종 복잡하게 얽힌 거대한 미로(maze)를 헤쳐 나가는 과정에 비유된다. 겉으로 드러난 단순한 인간의 실수 이면에 감추어진 잠재적 설계 결함, 부적절한 절차, 훈련 부족, 경영진의 생산 압박 등 복합적인 시스템적 유해위험요인들을 하나하나 끈기 있게 추적해 나가야 한다.

---

issues.en:
### INJURY MANAGEMENT PROCESS BOOKLET

The purpose of an Injury Management Process Booklet is to create a “Grab N Go Kit” so that all of the documents that are needed to capture the details of an injury, beginning with the circumstances that led to the injury and all of the fact(s) of what occurred (Create a Grab n Go-Kit & Effectively Manage Incidents, 2018) This Grab N Go Kit will include specific guidelines for investigators and information on how the process will be followed by employees, the leadership team, and medical providers. The guidelines would provide for the investigation of all types of incidents such as property or equipment damage, employee injury, vehicle accidents, third-party injury or damage, product or services losses.

A sample incident management booklet is provided for reference only and should be modified to meet the needs of an organization. Refer Appendix11.9 for the procedure and forms that can be used to capture and control all of the information that is needed to document the Injury Management Process. This booklet is considered a living document and must be updated with any discussions with the employee, the medical provider, any member of the leadership team, Human Resources, and so on. The key is that the booklet will become a permanent part of an employee’s record with any changes in condition or challenges.

The information collected by this procedure must be accurate, as it can assist in identifying the root cause analysis and corrective actions of any event, as well as preventive steps that will be taken to prevent recurrence.

The order of completion of the documents is crucial, based on the nature of the incident. The goal is to apply problemsolving methods with comprehensive reports to leadership consistently. The documentation of an incident should be completed logically to ensure all required information is timely and appropriately captured.

Refer Fig. 11.8 for a Sample process for managing and controlling injuries. This basic flow diagram is a suggested format that can be modified based on the organizational requirements.

### 부상 관리 프로세스 핸드북 (INJURY MANAGEMENT PROCESS BOOKLET)

사업장에서 인명 부상 사고가 발생했을 때 초기 대응의 혼선을 방지하고 피해를 최소화하기 위해 '부상 관리 프로세스 표준 책자'가 사전에 완벽히 구축되어 있어야 한다.

이와 관련된 모든 지침서와 서식은 반드시 최고 경영진, 법무팀, 리스크관리부서, 그리고 인사부서(HR)의 면밀한 사전 검토와 공식 승인을 거쳐 발행되어야 한다. 왜냐하면 그 어떤 손실 유발 사건이라 할지라도 막대한 운영적 타격, 심각한 법적 책임 소송, 혹은 정부의 가혹한 규제 제재를 초래할 수 있기 때문이다. 이 프로세스는 사내의 그 어떤 단체협약이나 계약 문서, 또는 공식 표준 절차를 침해하지 않도록 정교하게 설계되어야 하며, 각 부서의 고유한 요구사항을 완벽히 충족시킬 수 있어야 한다.

### LESSON LEARNED

> **Baseline Assessment**—The baseline assessment can be deceptively simple. Most organizations find when completing this inventory that they do not have a good grasp of the real scope and number of jobs being conducted. It is easy to overlook routine or nonroutine jobs. For example, some jobs may only be done when equipment requires maintenance and considered possible as little as only once per year. Also, routine jobs or activities can be on second or third shifts also missed during the inventory.

The critical point is to include employees in all phases of the JHA process and its development. Employee involvement in reviewing current job criteria as well as providing insights into the effectiveness of standard operating procedures (SOP) and training is critical to creating a useful process.

> Culture is created and sustained by a network of communications in which meaning is generated. The culture’s material embodiments include artifacts and written texts, through which meaning is passed on from generation to generation.  
> — *(Capra & Luisi, 2014)*

---

### 학습 교훈 (LESSON LEARNED)

직무 인벤토리를 작성할 때 관리자들은 종종 사무실에 앉아 형식적인 서류상의 직무 기술서만을 보고 목록을 만드는 치명적인 실수를 범한다. 그러나 현장의 실제 작업은 서류상의 기술서와는 완전히 다르게 돌아가는 경우가 허다하다. 근로자들은 현장의 설비 노후화, 작업 공간의 협소함, 부품의 치수 불량, 또는 촉박한 납기 압박을 극복하기 위해 나름의 비공식적인 작업 요령(workarounds)을 고안하여 작업하고 있기 때문이다. 이러한 현장의 '실제 작업 방식'을 온전히 반영하지 못한 채 책상머리에서 작성된 직무 인벤토리는 현장의 치명적인 숨은 위험을 완전히 놓쳐버리는 무용지물로 전락하게 된다. 따라서 관리감독자는 반드시 작업 현장에 직접 나가 실제 작업을 온몸으로 관찰하고 작업자와 긴밀히 대화하며 인벤토리를 완성해야 한다.

---

issues.en:
## WHY IS A JHA IMPORTANT?

JHAs provide an understanding of hazards at their point of beginning, where job tasks and activities are completed, and exposure to hazards are present. As a structured format, they can focus on specific problems or issues for immediate correction or relay to decision makers. The JHA increases the potential for removing administrative and job design obstacles hindering activities designed to reduce the consequences of loss-producing events.

The JHA further provides a consistent method for developing effective training programs highlighting desired safer and more efficient work methods. The JHA can be used as a comprehensive training aid to ensure employees know the primary requirements of each assignment and how to make safe choices best when performing specific tasks. Refer Table 12.1 to review a list of why JHAs are important (Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013).

The JHA process provides a better method to identify opportunities for improvement in the safety management system and provides the foundation for ongoing hazard and risk-based analysis. If a structured process is routinely followed, problems may be uncovered requiring the leadership team to make decisions if a specific task requires modification. By comprehensively and routinely using the JHA, a performance measurement system can be established to determine if jobs and activities are safely performed (Figs. 12.1 and 12.2).

---
issues.ko:
## JHA는 왜 중요한가? (WHY IS A JHA IMPORTANT?)

많은 기업들이 일상적으로 반복되는 작업에 대해 "이미 수년간 아무 사고 없이 해오던 일인데 굳이 번거롭게 JHA를 작성해야 하는가?"라는 회의적인 의문을 제기하곤 한다. 그러나 과거에 사고가 없었다고 해서 위험이 없다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다는 '무손실=무위험 신화'의 오류는 이미 앞선 장들에서 명백히 입증되었다.

JHA가 결정적으로 중요한 이유는 일상 업무의 당연한 관행 뒤에 은폐되어 있던 잠재 위험요인들을 과학적으로 분해하여 가시화해 주기 때문이다. JHA는 단순한 안전 점검을 넘어, 작업 절차의 표준화, 설비 개선, 교육 훈련 니즈 도출, 그리고 근골격계 질환과 같은 만성적 유해요인을 종합적으로 걸러내는 다목적 안전 나침반 역할을 수행한다 (표 12.1 참조).

---

issues.en:
## SELECTING A TEAM

As discussed in Chapter 8, Getting Employees Involved in the Safety Management System, an Ad Hoc Team can be established as part of the safety committee to help develop and review JHAs.

A team leader such as the safety professional or a member of the safety committee can be designated to guide and administer the JHA process. This person would use a cross-functional Ad Hoc Team to involve and maintain the knowledge and expertise for the development of a portfolio of JHAs. The JHA Ad Hoc Team would develop designated JHAs based on an initial hazard and risk assessment list produced from the job inventory. They would draw on experience and expertise of employees and supervisors in the department or area where the jobs are being completed.

Use of an Ad Hoc JHA team can promote a more efficient process and ensure that a variety of perspectives and opinions are considered. Using multiple teams allows quicker development and completion of JHAs. This approach spreads the time requirements through the organization and allows for more employee involvement. More involvement disseminates JHA expertise and increases the flow of safety-related information through the organization.

The individual selected to be the JHA process Ad Hoc team administrator should have a combination of the traits:
* Be a good representative of the JHA process and able to communicate verbally, in writing and provide updates on the process of leadership.
* Be able to communicate the value and benefits of the JHA process.
* Be knowledgeable about operations and understand the various production and service processes and methods used by the organization.
* Be able to apply risk assessment and problem-solving techniques to uncover hidden hazards and associated risk.
* Understand the nature and relationship of hazards and associated risk with potential loss-producing events.

This individual should have the communication and negotiation skills to overcome barriers or resistance to change that may occur during the implementation of JHAs and reinforce the leadership team’s commitment to the process. The JHA administrator would use a variety of methods and procedures to include:
* Providing input and advice to the Ad Hoc Teams developing JHAs.
* Assisting with evaluating the completeness and effectiveness of the JHAs based on job reviews, observations, and employee discussions.
* Assisting in using the JHAs in loss-producing events investigations and reviews.
* Assisting in the periodic evaluation of JHAs to ensure that they are using the current operational process, technology, task, and employee skill/training requirements.
* Assisting in reviewing the JHAs with employees to ensure that there is an understanding of what is expected of them and if they have any concerns about new procedures or actions required (Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013).

The Ad Hoc JHA Team was discussed in Chapter 8, Getting Employees Involved in the Safety Management System, but we wanted to reinforce the concepts as follows:
* Use a charter to define how they will operate and use the JHA Process. The charter would be authorized by the leadership team as approved by the central safety committee.
* Hold regular meetings and provide written documentation of meeting minutes to the JHA Process administrator on the central safety committee.
* Encourage employee involvement by communicating the value and use of JHAs.
* Analyze jobs, steps, and tasks to uncover hidden hazards and assess associated risk.
* Recommend feasible controls to reduce or eliminate identified hazards and associated risk to an acceptable level.
* Use a team approach to encourage different perspectives.
* Periodically evaluate the effectiveness of the JHA (Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013).

---

## JHA 전담 추진팀의 선발과 구성 (SELECTING A TEAM)

JHA를 가장 성공적으로 추진하기 위해서는 작업 현장에 정통한 다기능 핵심 인력들로 구성된 'JHA 특별 전담팀(Ad Hoc Team)'을 선발해야 한다. 이 전담팀은 특정 직무의 세부 과업을 가장 잘 이해하는 현장 근로자, 직속 관리감독자, 설비 정비를 책임지는 공무 기사, 그리고 사업장 안전 전문가로 구성된다.

JHA 특별 전담팀의 핵심 임무와 기능은 다음과 같다:
* JHA를 직접 개발하는 하위 태스크포스 팀들에게 전문적인 조언과 현장 피드백을 제공한다.
* 현장 직무 관찰, 작업 실사, 그리고 근로자와의 심층 인터뷰를 바탕으로 작성된 JHA의 완전성과 실효성을 엄격히 평가한다.
* 사업장에서 부상이나 아차사고 등 손실 유발 사건이 발생했을 때, 해당 JHA를 사고 조사 및 원인 규명의 기초 지침으로 적극 활용한다.
* JHA가 현재의 최신 운영 공정, 첨단 기술, 변경된 작업 과업, 그리고 근로자의 기술 및 훈련 요구수준을 제대로 반영하고 있는지 정기적으로 재평가하고 최신화한다.
* 개정된 JHA를 현장 근로자들과 함께 정밀 검토함으로써, 그들에게 기대되는 안전 행동이 무엇인지 확실히 이해시키고 새로운 작업 절차에 대한 고충과 우려 사항을 경청한다 (Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013).

JHA 특별 전담팀의 기본 운영 원칙은 다음과 같다:
* 팀의 운영 목적과 JHA 활용 방안을 명문화한 공식 '운영 헌장(charter)'을 수립하고 중앙 안전위원회의 공식 승인을 받는다.
* 정기적인 회의를 개최하고 회의록을 중앙 안전위원회의 JHA 총괄 간사에게 성실히 제출한다.
* JHA의 본질적 가치와 현장 활용법을 전파함으로써 근로자들의 자발적인 동참을 적극 독려한다.
* 직무, 단계, 과업을 치밀하게 분석하여 숨은 위험을 발굴하고 연계 위험을 정밀 평가한다.
* 식별된 위험을 사회적으로 용인 가능한 수준(ALARP)으로 낮추기 위한 실행 가능한 통제 대책을 권고한다.
* 다양한 직무 관점을 융합하기 위해 다기능 팀 접근법(cross-functional team approach)을 견지한다.
* 현장에 적용된 JHA의 실질적 유효성을 정기적으로 재평가한다 (Managing worker safety and health, 2016; Roughton & Crutchfield, 2013).

## APPENDIX 12.4 DRAFT COMPANY-WIDE LETTER TO IMPLEMENT KNIFE SAFETY AND CUT RESISTANT GLOVE PROGRAM

[Insert Company Name] conducted a risk assessment project regarding Knife Safety and Cut Resistant Glove to help
identify contributing factors and actions necessary to reduce the risk of laceration-type injuries. The purpose of the assess-
ments was to eliminate the use of knives wherever possible, specify lower risk cutting tools, and identify the proper level of
personal protection (cut resistant gloves) for specific tasks.
Based on the assessment, [Insert Company Name] has identified a selection of “approved” cut resistant gloves and
cutting tools matched to specific tasks being performed. The knives and gloves on the approved list were selected based
on findings from the on-site assessments that were conducted at a representative mix of locations.
To accomplish the implementation plan, each facility should implement and develop a specific plan as follows:
* Address the required use of proper tools and personal protective equipment (PPE) for the identified task. For any level of
PPE, Use the PPE assessment and other forms to document the initial assessment (PPE assessment, n.d.). Refer
Appendix 12.8 for a sample Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Assessment.
* Establish a schedule to complete implementation of the cutting tools and gloves programs. Refer Appendix 12.5
Sample Analysis of Self-Retractable Knives, and Appendix 12.7 Sample Analysis of Cut Resistant Gloves
Selection Guide.
* Provided the appropriate level of training employees on the new/updated procedures and in the proper use of the cutting
tools and cut resistance gloves. Refer Appendix 12.6 for a Sample Knife Safety Training Checklist.
* Distribute the cutting tools and cut resistance gloves to each required task. Eliminate the use of and remove the non-
approved equipment. For sites that currently purchase PPE from [insert vendor name], please ensure that these vendors
indicate a willingness to work with the sites on returning nonapproved knifes and cut resistant gloves in exchange for
approved gloves (at cost differential).
The Safety & Health Support team is available to assist in implementing these procedures.
Thank you in advance for your help in improving our safety programs.

[회사명 삽입]은 작업장 내 열상(베임) 재해의 위험을 근원적으로 줄이기 위해 필요한 핵심 기여 요인과 구체적 실행 조치를 규명하고자 '칼 안전 및 절단 방지 장갑에 관한 전사적 위험성 평가 프로젝트'를 실시하였습니다. 본 평가의 핵심 목적은 가능한 모든 작업에서 칼의 사용 자체를 원천 배제하고, 저위험 대체 절단 공구를 지정하며, 각 작업 과업별로 최적화된 적정 수준의 개인보호구(절단 방지 장갑)를 명확히 규정하는 데 있습니다.

본 정밀 평가 결과를 바탕으로, [회사명 삽입]은 실제 현장에서 수행되는 다양한 세부 과업들에 완벽히 부합하는 '공식 승인(approved)' 절단 방지 장갑 및 절단 공구 목록을 확정하였습니다. 승인 목록에 등재된 안전 칼과 보호 장갑은 회사의 대표적인 다양한 사업장 현장에서 실시된 실사 평가의 엄밀한 객관적 결과를 바탕으로 엄선되었습니다.

이 실행 계획을 성공적으로 완수하기 위해, 각 사업장은 다음과 같은 세부 현장 실천 계획을 즉시 수립하고 실행해야 합니다:
* 작업에 적합한 표준 공구와 필수 개인보호구의 의무적 착용 규정을 명확히 수립할 것.
* 위험에 노출된 모든 현장 작업자들에게 신형 안전 칼 조작법과 보호 장갑 관리 요령에 대한 실습 교육을 철저히 실시할 것.
* 기존의 위험한 일반 커터칼을 전량 수거하여 폐기하고 공인된 안전 칼로 100% 교체할 것.
* 현장 관리감독자의 일일 점검을 통해 임의적인 비공인 공구 반입을 엄격히 통제할 것.

본 도구는 현장 근로자들에게 구체적으로 어떤 개인보호구(PPE)가 필요한지 판별하기 위해 작업장 내의 잠재 유해위험요인을 신체 부위별로 체계적으로 식별할 수 있도록 지원한다. 유해 작업 활동들은 신체 부위별로 다음과 같이 범주화된다:
* **눈 및 안면 (Eyes and Face)**: 비산물, 분진, 용융 금속, 화학물질 액적 및 증기, 유해 광선(용접광 등).
* **머리 (Head)**: 낙하물, 상부 돌출 구조물 충돌, 감전 위험.
* **발 및 다리 (Feet and Legs)**: 중량물 낙하 및 구름, 날카로운 못 등 바닥 관통물, 화학물질 누출, 미끄러운 바닥.
* **손 및 팔 (Hands and Arms)**: 날카로운 칼날 절단, 타박상, 화학 화상, 극심한 온도, 감전.
* **호흡기 및 전신 (Respiratory & Body)**: 유독가스, 산소 결핍, 분진 흡입, 고온 복사열, 유해물질 오염.

issues.en: To be effective and timely, an assessment should be part of an overall strategy scheduled into your annual planning process. The assessment can be spread over time to make use of available windows of opportunity given all the other activities that must be completed by the leadership team members who should be involved.
issues.ko: 평가가 실질적인 유효성을 발휘하고 시의적절하게 이루어지기 위해서는, 조직의 전체적인 운영 전략 및 목표와 긴밀히 연계된 종합적 안전보건경영시스템 체계의 핵심 부분으로 자리매김해야 합니다.

issues.en: An assessment should include members drawn from the leadership team, safety committee members, and employees with specific knowledge of the topic under discussion. The best evaluators will be employees who can provide an unbiased and fresh look at the organization. While many employees will be candid in their comments, care must be taken to not shut down critical comments or discussions as these results in not getting the solid, honest feedback essential to any assessment.
issues.ko: 진단 평가는 경영진 리더십 팀과 일선 작업 현장 직원 중에서 선발된 다양한 계층의 구성원들로 평가팀을 구성해야 합니다. 다양한 시각을 가진 현장 인력이 참여할 때에만 편향되지 않은 객관적인 진단이 가능해집니다.

issues.en:
> Self-assessment is the formal or informal process of identifying one’s opportunities for improvement by comparing present practices and results with desired practices, results, and standards. Because no one knows better how things are done in the facility than those working in the performing organizations, self-assessments can be the most effective means of identifying latent weaknesses in the organization and the facility.  
> — *(Human performance tools for individuals, work teams, and management, 2009)*
issues.ko:
> "자체 평가(Self-assessment)란 조직이 사전에 정의된 표준에 대비하여 자신의 활동과 성과 수준을 스스로 식별하고 종합적으로 평가하는 공식적 또는 비공식적인 프로세스이다."  
> — (Department of Energy, 1999)

issues.en: To be consistent with your assessment, a customized self-assessment worksheet or checklist is used that covers all the core principles and the subelements that are to be considered under each principle. The key is to consistently use a regularly scheduled self-assessment to evaluate current performance and compare the results against the ideal or expected. The core safety management system elements, as provided in Table 14.1, Six Basic Core Principles of a Typical Management System, are reviewed using a self-assessment worksheet or checklist to provide a consistent, structured approach. Refer Appendix 14.1, Instructions for Using the Safety Management System Worksheet and Appendix 14.2, Attributes of a Safety Management System.
issues.ko: 평가의 일관성과 객관성을 유지하기 위해, 사전에 표준화된 맞춤형 자체 평가 도구(Customized self-assessment instrument)를 체계적으로 개발하여 활용해야 합니다. 표준 점검표가 없다면 평가자의 주관적 성향에 따라 결과가 들쑥날쑥해지며, 장기적인 추세 분석이 불가능해집니다.

issues.en:
## THIRD-PARTY ASSESSMENTS

Third-Party assessments are conducted by an outside resource selected or designed to provide an unbiased view of the system. While internal self-assessments are an essential part of the assessment process, an outside point of view or perspective can uncover or identify gaps that have been unconsciously overlooked by the internal assessment. The day-to-day familiarity with “how things get done around here” may have allowed the program to gradually drift away over the course of time from the initial guidelines and established standards. If the facility has completed an internal self-assessment, the independent review will serve as verification (calibration) of management commitment to safety.
issues.ko:
## 제3자 외부 평가 (THIRD-PARTY ASSESSMENTS)

제3자 평가는 조직 외부의 독립적인 전문 기관, 컨설팅 자문단, 본사 감사팀 또는 정부 공인 기관에 의해 수행되는 평가를 의미합니다. 내부 평가자가 일상적인 작업 환경에 너무 익숙해져 미처 발견하지 못하는 이른바 '친숙함의 맹점(Blind spots)'을 객관적인 시선으로 포착해 낼 수 있다는 결정적인 장점을 제공합니다.

issues.en:
> Reviews of facility activities by outside organizations or agencies provide an opportunity to reveal “blind spots” to facility management and personnel that could otherwise remain hidden. Independent oversight can identify conditions, processes, and practices that fall short of industry best practices and those that could lead to degraded facility performance if uncorrected.  
> — *(Human performance tools for individuals, work teams, and management, 2009)*
issues.ko:
> "외부 조직이나 전문 기관에 의해 실시되는 사업장 활동 검토는 객관적이고 독립적인 제3자의 관점을 제공하며, 이는 내부 인력들이 일상성에 매몰되어 간과하기 쉬운 시스템적 취약점을 규명하는 데 대단히 유용하다."  
> — (System safety training, 2000)

issues.en:
## PREASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES

Initial coordination is made with the location having a safety management system review. The preassessment is to begin the coordination with local leadership on the requirements of the assessment, its planning, and communication:
* Establish the dates and times of the assessment that are mutually acceptable to the local leadership and schedules of both the location and the assessment teams.
* Coordinate the assessment team for the available dates and times.
* Request the required documents and information to be available at the beginning of the assessment:
  * Background information about the location’s current activities and overall status.
  * Previous assessments, five years if possible, include internal and external other surveys or assessments by insurance loss control, other consultants, and so on.
  * Current policies, procedures, programs, job hazard analyses, inspection reports (machine/equipment checklist, property/facility specific), safety meetings and safety committee meetings, and so on.
  * Leadership and employees perception survey results.
  * History of loss-producing events—injuries, damage reports, near-misses, insurance claims reports (Workers’ Compensation, vehicle, liability, property, incident investigations).
issues.ko:
## 사전 평가 준비 활동 (PREASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES)

현장 방문에 앞서 대상 사업장과의 긴밀한 사전 조율이 이루어져야 합니다. 평가의 구체적인 목적, 일정표, 필요한 서류 목록, 그리고 인터뷰 대상자 명단을 미리 공유함으로써 현장의 혼선을 방지하고 평가의 효율성을 극대화할 수 있습니다.

issues.en: Safety perception surveys are an important tool used to ask questions employees can answer anonymously and in confidence. They provide the ability to measure the answers to questions and summarize responses. They can provide statistical validation of the perceptions of employees about the safety culture. Surveys must be carefully selected and structured to prevent personal bias and a skewing of the responses.
issues.ko: 안전문화 인식도 설문조사(Safety perception surveys)는 경영진과 근로자 모두에게 구조화된 질문을 던져 현장의 실제 안전문화 상태에 대한 솔직한 인식을 파악할 수 있는 대단히 가치 있는 핵심 사전 도구입니다.

issues.en: Refer Appendix 14.3, “Safety Management Perception Questionnaire” for an example of a perception survey, an instrument developed by Bob Lapidus and Dr. Michael Waite. This perception survey is a tested and validated format which has been used to identify safety program opinion differences between leadership and employees (Lapidus & Waite, 2013).
issues.ko: 사내 안전문화 진단에 즉시 활용할 수 있는 포괄적인 설문 문항 양식은 부록 14.3의 “안전경영 인식도 설문지(Safety Management Perception Questionnaire)”를 참조하십시오.

issues.en:
## THE OPENING MEETING

The opening meeting is used to discuss with the local leadership team and employees the purpose, scope, intent, and activities that will be needed for the Assessment:
* Discuss the objectives and scope of the assessment and its intent.
* Discuss the assessment process, checklists/forms, and the resources needed, schedule of interviews, employee group meetings, focus groups, and so on.
* Introduce assessment team members and share expertise and skills.
* Discuss personal safety considerations, for example, personal protective equipment, visitor guidelines, escort areas, security clearances, and so on.
* Establish communication, media to use (internet, Skype, e-mails, and so on), develop a schedule based on activities, timing.
* Develop schedule and agenda for the closing meeting.
issues.ko:
## 킥오프 시작 회의 (THE OPENING MEETING)

시작 회의(Opening meeting)는 현장 사업장의 경영진 리더십 팀 및 주요 부서장들과 공식적으로 마주 앉아 이번 진단 평가의 취지, 범위, 세부 일정, 그리고 전반적인 평가 방법론을 상호 명확히 공유하고 합의하기 위해 개최됩니다.

issues.en:
## SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM ASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES

Activities involved in the Assessment of a safety management system include:
* An initial tour to become familiar with the nature of operations, worksites, facilities.
* Review requested documents and materials provided.
* Begin process using more in-depth observations of activities, specific high hazard jobs, general environment.
* Interview employees during observations.
issues.ko:
## 안전보건경영시스템 평가의 핵심 활동 (SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM ASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES)

본격적인 현장 진단 평가 활동은 다음의 4대 핵심 축을 중심으로 유기적으로 진행됩니다:
1. 사업장 전체에 대한 초기 현장 라운딩 (Initial Location Tour)
2. 사내 규정, 기록 및 지표에 대한 서류 심사 (Document Reviews)
3. 리더십 및 현장 근로자와의 심층 인터뷰 (Leadership and Employee Interviews)
4. 작업 환경 및 현장 안전 조건에 대한 정밀 관찰 (Review of Site Conditions)

issues.en: As we have stressed throughout this book, any activity that is undertaken must be considered as having the potential for either improving or degrading the safety culture of the organization. The methods used for coordination and the completion of the assessment must be conducted in a manner that is seen as professional, organized, respectful, and considered of value to the location’s leadership team and employees. An assessment has the potential to be seen as critical of the leadership team and if not communicated and presented properly may create issues within the organization.
issues.ko: 우리가 이 책 전체를 통해 끊임없이 강조해 왔듯이, 안전 전문가나 평가팀이 수행하는 모든 활동은 궁극적으로 안전에 대한 긍정적 지각을 고양하고, 조직 내에서 영향력을 확대하며, 강력한 의사소통 네트워크를 확장하는 데 기여해야 합니다.

issues.en: During walk-through of work areas the assessment team would interview employees one-on-one in their work area about their training and perceptions of the safety management system. Any topic is acceptable if it leads to a better understanding of problems or concerns about the workplace. If safety-related training is effective, employees will be able to describe the hazards inherent in their work and the effectiveness of the controls that are in place. In this discussion, an indicator of the depth of the safety culture is how well employees can describe what is expected of them in any safety-related activities.
issues.ko: 작업 구역 워크스루 순찰 중에 평가팀은 현장 작업자들과 자연스럽게 대화를 나누며, 안전 장비 사용의 편의성, 작업 전 위험성 평가의 실효성, 그리고 관리감독자의 안전 코칭 태도에 대한 생생한 피드백을 수집합니다.

issues.en: For example, employees’ perceptions and opinions about the ease or difficulty in reporting hazards and the time it takes to get a response will validate the effectiveness of any hazard reporting system. If employees indicate that the system for enforcing safety rules and work practices is inconsistent or confusing, a gap in this system element is identified.
issues.ko: 예를 들어, 위험을 보고하거나 개선을 제안하는 사내 절차가 얼마나 쉽고 접근하기 편리한지에 대한 작업자들의 지각과 솔직한 의견은 안전보건경영시스템의 실질적 건강성을 판별하는 매우 강력한 시금석이 됩니다.

issues.en:
## COMMUNICATION AND FEEDBACK

The assessment team leader is the focal point of all information collected by team members and will provide updates to the leadership on the assessment process. If potential high severity hazards and associated risks are identified, the assessment is stopped, and the problem/issue is immediately relayed to leadership for corrective actions. At the end of each day or work shift, a meeting should be held with the leadership team and employees to update findings, additional documentation needs, and immediate concerns about the assessment.
issues.ko:
## 의사소통 및 일일 피드백 (COMMUNICATION AND FEEDBACK)

평가팀 리더는 현장 사업장 경영진과의 단일 공식 소통 창구 역할을 수행합니다. 평가 기간 동안 매일 일정이 종료될 때마다, 평가팀은 당일 관찰된 주요 사실과 긍정적인 모범 사례, 그리고 시급한 개선 필요 사항을 사업장 리더십에게 간략히 브리핑하는 '일일 디브리핑(Daily Debrief)'을 진행해야 합니다.

issues.en:
## REVIEW OF SITE CONDITIONS

The review of site conditions can provide a strong indicator of the true safety culture of the organization. If the documentation shows that inspections are routinely completed, yet the conditions indicate uncontrolled hazards and associated risks are present, then a gap exists between what the organization espouses and what beliefs and norms are actually in place.
issues.ko:
## 현장 안전 조건의 검토 (REVIEW OF SITE CONDITIONS)

물리적 현장 작업 조건에 대한 정밀 검토는 안전보건경영시스템이 서류상으로만 존재하는 것이 아니라 실제 현장에서 얼마나 충실하게 이행되고 있는지를 검증하는 가시적 척도를 제공합니다.

issues.en:
## PRESENTING RESULTS OF THE SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM ASSESSMENT

The methods for presenting the findings of the assessment should be determined in the initial planning meeting with a clearly defined format, style, and structure. The structure should follow the outline of the safety management system’s content to be consistent over time. A wide range of methods can be used that can involve either quantitative and qualitative information. A scoring method is usually followed to allow a measurement of the finding along with a predetermined scale.
issues.ko:
## 평가 결과의 발표 및 최종 보고 (PRESENTING RESULTS OF THE SAFETY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM ASSESSMENT)

진단 평가 결과를 공식 발표할 때는 비판이나 지적 위주가 아닌, 현장의 노력에 대한 격려와 미래의 실질적 개선 방향을 제시하는 '건설적이고 긍정적인 톤'을 유지해야 합니다.

issues.en:
## COMMUNICATING THE ASSESSMENT AND THE ACTION PLANS

Throughout the assessment, members of leadership and employees will have been involved in the meetings, discussions, reviews, and observations. It is important that all employees be provided with the results of the assessment, its findings, recommendations, and the action plan that has been developed. In our experience, too often, employee involvement is not recognized by a sharing of information. After the action plan has been developed, the findings must be communicated by:
* Providing a summary of the final assessment report.
* Providing information on how the assessment was completed and who was involved.
* Listing the assessment findings and opportunities for improvement.
* Sharing the action plan that may have resulted from the assessment.
issues.ko:
## 평가 결과 및 실행 계획의 전사적 소통 (COMMUNICATING THE ASSESSMENT AND THE ACTION PLANS)

이 책 전체를 통틀어 누차 역설해 왔듯이, 투명한 의사소통은 신뢰 구축의 절대적인 초석입니다. 경영진은 인터뷰와 설문에 참여했던 모든 직원들에게 평가를 통해 무엇이 발견되었고, 회사가 앞으로 어떤 구체적인 조치를 취할 것인지를 숨김없이 공유해야 합니다.

issues.en:
## EXAMPLE ASSESSMENT AND ACTION PLAN

Refer Appendix 14.4 for an Example Safety Management System Assessment and Action Plan Strategy which is an outline providing the various activities to be included in the assessment of a safety management system. It follows a strategy, measurement, an outline of how the assessment would be organized, the metrics required, and how hazards and associated risk would be treated.
issues.ko:
## 진단 평가 및 실행 계획의 실제 사례 (EXAMPLE ASSESSMENT AND ACTION PLAN)

실제 산업 현장에 즉시 적용할 수 있는 구체적인 안전보건경영시스템 진단 평가 및 액션 플랜의 표준 예시는 부록 14.4를 참조하십시오.

issues.en:
## ASSESSMENT EXAMPLES

There are several excellent self-assessment tools that are available to help with assessing the Safety Management System. These assessment tools are public domain documents that can be downloaded and used for your library:
* “Worksheets and a Rating Tool to Help Strengthen Jobsite Safety Climate” (2016) — Refer Appendix 14.5.
* “Safety and Health Program Audit Tool” as outlined in the Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs General Industry, OSHA 3885 (2016) — Refer Appendix 14.6.
issues.ko:
## 유용한 진단 평가 도구 예시 (ASSESSMENT EXAMPLES)

시중에는 OSHA의 SHARP(Safety and Health Achievement Recognition Program) 워크시트, VPP(자율안전프로그램) 자체 평가 도구 등 안전보건 전문가들이 벤치마킹하여 자사에 맞게 커스터마이징할 수 있는 수많은 탁월한 공개 평가 프레임워크들이 존재합니다.

issues.en:
## SUMMARY

* A Safety Management System assessment provides a comprehensive assessment of the current state of the safety culture.
* The safety management system should reflect the real values and beliefs of the organization.
* The full implementation of a safety management system provides the structure to guide decisions and activities for the long-term success of a safety culture.
* As discussed in several other chapters, an effort should be made to assess and change as necessary the perception of safety, extend safety leadership influence within the organization, and expand the internal safety network, all for the benefit of the organization. A personal assessment should verify how goals are accomplished as well as the implementation of the safety management system.
* The understanding should be developed that a safety management system assessment goes beyond just physical reviews such as the traditional facility inspections.
* Inspections are critical and valuable in reviewing facilities to identify and eliminate or control hazards.
* An efficient and timely assessment should be part of an overall strategy scheduled for the annual planning process.
* An assessment should include members drawn from the leadership team, safety committee members, and employees with knowledge about the topic under discussion.
* By maintaining a diverse perspective, the different experiences, skills, and expertise can bring additional insights. The team members should be rotated using a percentage of new members for each assessment.
* The preassessment is to begin the coordination with local leadership on the requirements of the assessment, its planning, and communication.
* The initial meeting is used to refresh the local leadership team and employees on the purpose, scope, intent, and activities that will be needed for the Assessment.
* The review of the location’s documentation determines the scope and quality of each of the activities required by the safety management system in use. The documentation should provide a comprehensive and clear picture of how the location has been administering and managing the system.
* The assessment team leader is the focal point of all information from the team and provides location leadership with updates on the assessment process.
* The review of site conditions may be a reliable indicator of the organization’s existing safety culture.
* Opportunities and obstacles to improvement are discussed with the assessment team after the leadership team has reviewed the gaps identified using the assessment.
* In Chapter 15, we will shift our focus from safety culture and discuss how a professional should become a curator for the safety management system. We will discuss how there is a desire for wanting information immediately and how library and curation methodology and structure should be adapted to organize all of the various media used to accomplish assigned tasks and responsibilities.
* This reinforces the common theme of communication as presented throughout the book. The key is that the safety management system and safety culture are dependent on the leadership team and employees maintaining open lines of communication and the delivery of impartial and factual messages.
issues.ko:
## 요약 (SUMMARY)

* 안전보건경영시스템 평가는 안전경영 활동의 실태, 행정적 통제 수준 및 실질적 유효성에 대한 포괄적이고 객관적인 검증을 제공합니다.
* 조직의 문화는 일상 과업을 수행하는 직원들의 규범, 습관, 행동에 지대한 영향을 미칩니다.
* 강력한 안전문화를 구현하기 위해 조직은 안전보건경영시스템의 긍정적 가치를 전사적으로 강조해야 하며, 지속적 학습과 평가의 중요성에 대한 확고한 신념을 내재화해야 합니다.
* 안전문화는 학습 조직의 산물입니다. 유해위험요인과 관련 위험성이 식별됨에 따라, 이를 선제적으로 통제하는 역량이 안전 성공의 핵심 열쇠가 됩니다.
* 평가 기획 시 일방적인 시스템 교체보다는 현 시스템 내부의 오류와 결함을 찾아 정밀하게 수선하는 6시그마적 접근법을 견지해야 합니다 ("시스템 탓하기" 지양).
* 진단 평가는 시작 회의, 현장 라운딩, 서류 검토, 심층 인터뷰, 작업 조건 관찰, 그리고 건설적인 최종 보고의 체계적 절차를 거쳐야 합니다.
* Newell(2001)이 지적했듯이, 전통적인 OSHA 재해율과 같은 단일 지표에 의존하는 것은 실패를 부추기며, 다양한 선행 지표와 프로세스 지표를 균형 있게 활용해야 합니다.
* 평가의 진정한 완성은 구체적이고 측정 가능한 SMART 액션 플랜을 수립하고, 이를 현장 직원들과 신속하고 투명하게 공유하여 신뢰를 공고히 하는 데 있습니다.

issues.en:
#### 1. The Leadership Team
* Top management policy establishes clear priority for safety and health
* Top management considers safety and health to be a line rather than a staff function
* Top management provides competent safety and health staff support to line managers and supervisors
* Managers personally follow safety and health rules
* Managers delegate the authority necessary for personnel to carry out their assigned safety and health responsibilities effectively
* Managers allocate the resources needed to properly support the organization's safety and health system
* Managers support fair and effective policies that promote safety and health performance
* Managers assure that appropriate safety and health training is provided
* Top management is involved in the planning and evaluation of safety and health performance
* Top management values employee involvement and participation in safety and health issues
issues.ko:
#### 1. 경영진 리더십 팀 (The Leadership Team)
* 최고경영진의 안전보건 방침이 명확한 비전과 우선순위를 확립하고 있는가?
* 안전보건 관련 목표 및 구체적 세부 추진 목표가 명확히 설정되어 있는가?
* 안전보건경영시스템을 운영하기 위한 충분한 인력, 예산, 시설 자원이 배정되어 있는가?
* 경영진이 일상 업무에서 솔선수범하여 안전 행동을 실천하고 모범을 보이는가?
* 모든 계층의 관리감독자에게 안전 책무(Accountability)가 명확히 부여되고 평가되는가?

issues.en:
#### 2. Employee Involvement
* There is an effective process to involve employees in safety and health issues
* Employees are involved in organizational decision making regarding safety and health policy
* Employees are involved in organizational decision making regarding the allocation of safety and health resources
* Employees are involved in organizational decision making regarding safety and health training
* Employees participate in hazard detection activities
* Employees participate in hazard prevention and control activities
* Employees participate in the safety and health training of coworkers
* Employees participate in safety and health planning activities
* Employees participate in the evaluation of safety and health performance
issues.ko:
#### 2. 근로자 참여 (Employee Involvement)
* 근로자가 안전보건 의사결정 및 개선 활동에 적극 참여할 수 있는 실효성 있는 프로세스가 존재하는가?
* 현장 위험 요인 및 아차사고를 두려움 없이 즉시 보고할 수 있는 무비난 열린 채널이 운영되는가?
* 안전보건위원회 또는 현장 안전 협의체가 정기적으로 활발하게 가동되는가?
* 작업자가 급박한 위험 직면 시 작업을 자율적으로 중지할 수 있는 '작업중지권(Stop Work Authority)'이 보장되는가?
* 근로자들이 사내 안전 활동에 개인적인 책임감을 갖고 주인의식을 발휘하는가?

issues.en:
#### 3. Risk and Hazard Identification and Assessment
* A comprehensive, baseline hazard survey has been conducted within the past five (5) years
* Effective safety and health self-inspections are performed regularly
* Effective surveillance of established hazard controls is conducted
* An effective hazard reporting system exists
* Change analysis is performed whenever a change in facilities, equipment, materials, or processes occurs
* Accidents are investigated for root causes
* Material Safety Data Sheets are used to reveal potential hazards associated with chemical products in the workplace
* Effective job hazard analysis is performed
* Expert hazard analysis is performed
* Incidents are investigated for root causes
issues.ko:
#### 3. 위험 및 유해위험요인 식별과 평가 (Risk and Hazard Identification and Assessment)
* 전 공정 및 작업에 대한 종합적인 초기 위험성 평가가 체계적으로 완료되었는가?
* 직무 위험 분석(JHA/JSA)이 모든 고위험 작업에 대해 수립되고 표준작업절차(SOP)에 반영되었는가?
* 신규 설비 도입, 공정 변경, 원자재 변경 시 변경관리(MOC) 절차가 철저히 가동되는가?
* 주기적인 현장 안전 순찰 및 점검이 누락 없이 실행되고 있는가?
* 사고 및 아차사고에 대한 근본 원인 분석(Root Cause Analysis)이 신속하고 엄밀하게 이루어지는가?

issues.en:
#### 4. Hazard Prevention and Control
* Feasible engineering controls are in place
* Effective safety and health rules and work practices are in place
* Applicable OSHA-mandated programs are effectively in place
* Personal protective equipment is effectively used
* Housekeeping is properly maintained
* The organization is properly prepared for emergencies
* The organization has an effective plan for providing competent emergency medical care to employees and others present at the site
* Effective preventive maintenance is performed
* An effective procedure for tracking hazard correction is in place
issues.ko:
#### 4. 유해위험요인의 예방 및 통제 (Hazard Prevention and Control)
* 위험 통제 시 위험 통제 계층구조(제거-대체-공학적 대책-관리적 대책-PPE)를 엄격히 준수하는가?
* 기계 방호 장치, 국소배기장치 등 실행 가능한 공학적 제어 설비가 완벽히 설치 및 유지관리되는가?
* 안전한 작업 방법과 표준작업절차가 현장 언어로 명문화되어 교육되는가?
* 정기적인 설비 예방 보전(Preventive maintenance) 프로그램이 철저히 실행되는가?
* 비상 대응 계획(Emergency Action Plan)이 수립되고 정기 실전 대피 훈련이 실시되는가?
* 적합한 개인보호구(PPE)가 무상 지급되고 올바른 착용 실태가 상시 감독되는가?

issues.en:
#### 5. Education and Training
* Employees receive appropriate safety and health training
* New employee orientation includes applicable safety and health information
* Supervisors receive appropriate safety and health training
* Supervisors receive training that covers the supervisory aspects of their safety and health responsibilities
* Safety and health training is provided to managers
* Relevant safety and health aspects are integrated into management training
issues.ko:
#### 5. 교육 및 훈련 (Education and Training)
* 모든 신규 입사자, 보직 변경자 및 하도급 협력업체 근로자가 작업 투입 전 필수 안전 교육을 이수하는가?
* 관리감독자와 현장 리더들이 유해위험요인 식별 및 안전 코칭 기법에 대한 전문 교육을 받는가?
* 교육 내용이 성인 학습 원리에 부합하며 현장 실무와 밀착되도록 설계되었는가?
* 근로자가 교육 내용을 완벽히 이해했는지를 검증하는 실효성 있는 평가가 실시되는가?
* 모든 교육훈련 이수 기록이 법정 서식에 맞추어 체계적으로 보존 및 관리되는가?

issues.en:
#### 6. Performance and Measurement
* Workplace injury/illness data are effectively analyzed
* Hazard incidence data are effectively analyzed
* A safety and health goal and supporting objectives exist
* An action plan designed to accomplish the organization's safety and health objectives is in place
* A review of in-place OSHA-mandated programs is conducted at least annually
* A review of the overall safety and health management system is conducted at least annually
* Safety and health program tasks are each specifically assigned to a person or position for performance or coordination
* Each assignment of safety and health responsibility is clearly communicated
* An accountability mechanism is included with each assignment of safety and health responsibility
* Individuals with assigned safety and health responsibilities have the necessary knowledge, skills, and timely information to perform their duties
* Individuals with assigned safety and health responsibilities have the authority to perform their duties
* Individuals with assigned safety and health responsibilities have the resources to perform their duties
* Organizational policies promote the performance of safety and health responsibilities
* Organizational policies result in correction of nonperformance of safety and health responsibilities
issues.ko:
#### 6. 성과 측정 및 지속적 평가 (Performance and Measurement)
* 사업장의 재해 데이터뿐만 아니라 선행 활동 지표가 균형 있게 추적 및 모니터링되는가?
* 안전보건경영시스템에 대한 전면적인 정기 진단 평가가 매년 1회 이상 체계적으로 실시되는가?
* 평가 결과 도출된 시정 조치들이 정해진 기한 내에 100% 완료되도록 사후 추적되는가?
* 안전 성과 결과가 최고경영진 회의에 정기적으로 공식 보고되고 피드백되는가?
* 과거의 재해 교훈과 평가 결과가 미래의 안전 계획 및 경영 방침에 능동적으로 환류되는가?
